items.name: Kit foundations — tokens, densities, materials, motion
items.purpose: The single declaration every other item in this kit references, so no component invents a value.
items.anatomy:
SPACE s1–s11 = 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 56, 72, 96. No other number exists in the kit.

DENSITY. Console: gutter 20 (40 at ≥1080dp), row min-height 44, block gap 24 (s7), intra-block 12 (s3). Field: gutter 20, row min-height 64, block gap 32 (s8), intra-block 16 (s4), tap ≥48, primary action 56. Veld: single density (TiqSkin.veld() takes no density argument), gutter 24 (s6), row min-height 64, block gap 40 (s9), tap ≥56.

RADII — five materials. r0 = rules, dividers, all Veld surfaces. r6 = chips, glyph tiles. r10 = buttons, thumbnails, input bottom corners. r14 = panel, sheet, form, soft row. r20 = photographic plate. r-pill = 999, reinstated by owner decision 3 and legal on exactly three objects: the floating nav bar, its active tab, the nav circle. Inputs are r10 at the BOTTOM corners, 0 at the top.

DEPTH — L0 ground (#0B1017 / #EEE9DF / #FFFFFF). L1 well (#141D27 / #E2DBCC). L2 surface (#1B2632 / #FAF7F2). L3 raised (#22303E / #F4F0E8). L4 emitted — a fill plus an amber alpha gradient, allocated by TorchScope.

DEVICE-FLOOR RULE — REWRITTEN, AND THIS IS THE REVISION THAT TOUCHES THE MOST COMPONENTS. Measured on the real hexes: well on ground is 1.12:1, surface on ground 1.24:1, lifted on ground 1.67:1, raised on surface 1.14:1. Every one of those is below what a 6-bit LCD at 40% backlight resolves. The first draft said 'identity is geometry, not fill' and then used an 8dp gap of ground between two invisible rows as the identifier — which is circular, because a gap is only a gap between two things you can see. THE RULE NOW: in Night, ANY object whose boundary must be perceived carries a real 1px edge — edge-structure #5A7088 for containers (3.73:1 on ground, 3.33:1 on well, 3.00:1 on surface) or edge-control #7C93AC for controls (6.02:1 on ground, 5.37:1 on well). Fill steps and gaps express GROUPING and HIERARCHY; edges express IDENTITY. Day carries identity on shadow plus fill, which works on a light ground. Veld carries it on a 2px #1B2632 border.

OPACITY IS BANNED AS A STATE CHANNEL — NEW, and it retires the 0.6/0.8/0.35 convention across six components. No widget in this kit may express a state by wrapping itself in Opacity or by an alpha multiplier on a token, because the CI contrast walk reads token pairs and cannot see a multiplier applied at the widget layer. Where a composited value is genuinely wanted as DECORATION, its flattened hex is declared as a token and tested like any other: wash-bad-night #302933 (bad@12% on well), wash-good-night #2A373D, press-ghost-night #18212D (lifted@40% on ground), rim-night #303A43 (Palladian@10% on surface), grabber-night #616465, plate-disc-worst #1D2025 (abyss-000@70% over the plate's #474747 ceiling; ink-1 on it is 13.5:1, which is the worst case any glyph over a plate can encounter). Every one of those is decoration; none is the sole signal for anything.

SHADOW — Night has zero BoxShadow. Day has sh1 0 1 2 rgba(27,38,50,.06), sh2 0 4 12 rgba(27,38,50,.08), sh3 0 12 32 rgba(27,38,50,.12), ≤6 per screen. Veld has none.

TYPE — Onest variable for every word; JetBrains Mono Medium for every figure in a data role and every machine identifier. Onest has no width axis, so the direction's wdth 88–112 instructions are void and weight plus tracking carry the display voice. hero.figure JBM 72/700/0.92/−2.5% (textScaler capped 1.6, the one documented exception, and above it the role swaps to hero.figure.compact rather than clipping). hero.figure.compact JBM 56/700/0.95. display Onest 40/700/1.00/−1.5%. figure.l JBM 32/600/1.05. figure.m JBM 22/600/1.10. figure.s JBM 16/600/1.20. title.l Onest 20/600/1.25 (24 in Field). title.m Onest 16/600/1.30. body Onest 15/400/1.50 Field, 14/400/1.55 Console. body.strong 600. label Onest 13/500/1.35/+0.5%. eyebrow Onest 11/700/1.10/+8% uppercase, ink-2, two roles only. meta Onest 12/400/1.40, ink-3. mono.ident JBM 13/500/1.30/+1%. Every figure role carries FontFeature.tabularFigures(). Veld steps: body 17, label 16, meta 14, title.m 18, title.l 22, figure.m 24, figure.s 18, weight floor 600, line-height +0.05, tracking +0.5%.

MOTION — 120 press/toggle/chip, 200 element enter (40 stagger), 320 sheet/route/plate, 600 count-up and busy dots, 1400 skeleton rule, 3200 live pulse. Curves: enter cubic-bezier(.05,.70,.10,1), exit (.30,0,.80,.15), state (.20,0,0,1), count-up ease-out-quart. ONE app-wide Ticker, three subscribers. Killed by MediaQuery.disableAnimations, battery saver, and Veld.
items.states: Not a rendered thing; it has no states. Its three skin factories are TiqSkin.night(density), TiqSkin.day(density), TiqSkin.veld().
items.behaviour: MediaQuery.textScaler clamped to 2.0 app-wide. SKIN CHANGES ARE AN INSTANT SET IN ALL THREE DIRECTIONS — REVISED. The first draft cross-faded Night↔Day at 320ms and instant-set only into Veld. The critic is right on both counts and I had the argument in my own hand: a whole-theme cross-fade rasterises two full widget trees into an offscreen layer, which is the one saveLayer the frame budget says does not exist, and 320ms of a half-lit screen is exactly as unreadable walking out of a cold room into a forecourt as it is walking into the sun. The cross-fade is deleted. Skin is a rebuild, not a transition.
items.modes: Night is the reference implementation. Day re-points the same token names at the light column. Veld replaces the token set, flattens every radius to 0 except r-pill, deletes every gradient, rim and shadow, and admits no text token below 9:1 and no border below 15:1.
items.accessibility: All contrast pairings are generated by a Dart test walking the three factories; CI fails if any declared pairing drops below its floor, and a greyscale plus Viénot deuteranopia/protanopia pass asserts minimum separation on every chart-series and state pair. The opacity ban is what makes that claim true rather than aspirational — before it, six components expressed states the walk could not see.
items.amber: none — this is the token sheet. Allocation lives in the Torch precedence pattern below.
items.screenshot: A specimen sheet: three columns headed NIGHT, DAY, VELD, each showing the same five swatches, four radii drawn as outlined squares, and the type scale set in Onest with the figures visibly monospaced and aligned in a column.

items.name: Torch precedence (TorchScope)
items.purpose: Allocates the screen's amber at runtime by fixed precedence, so the law is enforced by the framework rather than asserted in prose — the blocker fix.
items.anatomy:
REPLACES the first draft's per-component amber ledger, which summed to three amber objects on the agent's home screen in Night and to two on a light ground, breaking the direction's amberResolution clause 2 by name. The kit even wrote the correct rationale for Day's ink nav tab and then handed the circle an amber block anyway.

TorchScope is an InheritedWidget at the top of every route. It takes a CLAIM SET computed by the route's view model — not by the widgets — because every overflow is runtime-conditional: whether a primary commit exists, whether the plate's bytes loaded, whether the circle's action is the expected next move, whether anything is genuinely sending, whether the answer has a focus bar. A view model can see all of that; a static lint can see none of it, which is why the first draft's lint was green on the exact screens that broke.

GRANTS: 2 in Night, 1 in Day and Veld.

PRECEDENCE, fixed and total: (1) primary commit action, (2) plate strip light, (3) chart focus fill — the one bar the answer's sentence is about, (4) nav circle, admissible ONLY on a route with no primary commit action, (5) live pulse, at most one instance per route on the first live row in view, (6) meter headline target tick.

CHROME IS NOT IN THE LADDER — and this is where I depart from the critic. He proposes the nav active tab yield to the primary per route. I will not do that: the nav is the app's permanent furniture, and furniture that is amber on Today and ink on Map reads as a rendering bug, not as a law. Instead, in NIGHT the nav active tab holds a reserved chrome grant whenever the nav renders, and content therefore has exactly one grant on a tabbed route and two where the nav is absent — inside a visit, in a sheet, in a dialog, in a full-screen state. That makes the law a sentence an agent could learn without being told: the torch is in your hand and on the shelf, one each. In DAY and VELD the chrome grant does not exist — the active tab is an ink block — and the single grant goes down the ladder.

API: TorchScope(grants:, claims: Set<TorchClaim>, subject: TorchClaim?, child:). granted(claim) is a pure function of the declared set, so resolution is deterministic and independent of build order. `subject` is the one declared override: it promotes a single claim above the primary, it must be written at the route's build so it is greppable and visible in code review, and the debug overlay prints it. It exists for the Ask TradeIQ answer route, where the send field is a commit action but the answer is the reason the user is there.
items.states: RESOLVED — every claim in the set is either granted or denied, and every denied claim renders the ink fallback it already owns: the circle becomes lifted with a rim and a filled-arrow glyph, the tab pill becomes the Day ink block, the plate renders without its strip light, the live pulse becomes a static filled square plus the word 'Live', the meter tick becomes ink-1 with its unchanged silhouette. Nothing is ever lost — the non-colour channel always carried the meaning. OVER-CLAIMED IN DEBUG: throws with the full claimant list and the route name, at build, on the developer's machine and in every widget test. OVER-CLAIMED IN RELEASE: silently denies from the bottom of the ladder, so the screen degrades rather than lying. UNDECLARED CLAIM: a component calling granted() for a claim the route did not declare asserts in debug — this is the case that catches a widget lighting something the route never knew about. ZERO CLAIMS: legal and common. Most screens in this app have one amber object and many have none.
items.behaviour: Resolution happens once per route build. A claim set that changes mid-route — the outbox starts sending, the circle becomes expected — rebuilds the scope and re-resolves; a claimant losing its grant cross-fades to its ink fallback at 200ms/state so nothing blinks. The lint rule survives but is narrowed to what a static analyser can actually see: Burning Flame assigned to a property the per-skin rule forbids — a fill on a light ground outside a registered primary, an icon tint, a chip background, text on a light ground that is not flame-300.
items.modes: Night: 2 grants, one reserved for chrome. Day: 1 grant, no chrome grant. Veld: 1 grant, no chrome grant, and in practice it is nearly always the primary commit block.
items.accessibility: This pattern is what makes 'colour is never the only signal' survivable: because any claimant can be denied at runtime, every claimant is REQUIRED to ship a complete non-colour treatment, and the denial path is exercised in golden tests. A design where amber is load-bearing would fail here; this one does not.
items.amber: it is the allocator. It holds all of it.
items.screenshot: A debug overlay in the corner of a dark screen listing 'claims: primary, plate, circle, live · grants 2 · granted: navTab(chrome), primary · denied: plate, circle, live' in small monospaced type.

items.name: Surface (Panel)
items.purpose: The one panel material, for exactly three things: an AI answer's instrument cluster, a form, and a sheet body.
items.anatomy: Night: fill abyss-200 #1B2632, radius 14 (r14), 1px edge-structure #5A7088 outline (3.00:1 on its own fill, 3.73:1 on ground), 1px rim-night #303A43 inset top rim drawn over the outline as declared decoration, padding 16 (s4), no shadow. Day: fill #FAF7F2, radius 14, 1px #857C6B outline, sh1. Veld: fill #FFFFFF, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border (15.33:1), padding 24 (s6). Internal divisions are 1px hairline-decorative #3A4B60 / #DED7C9 full-bleed to the panel edge (Veld: 2px #1B2632), never a gap — a hairline says 'same instrument, next cell'; a gap says 'different object'.
items.states: Default. Interactive (whole panel tappable): pressed adds a lifted #2C3B4D fill and 0.98 scale, 120ms. Loading: see Loading skeleton, drawn inside the same outline at the same geometry so nothing moves on arrival. Empty: the panel does not render at all — an outlined box around nothing is a claim that data exists. Error: outline swaps to 1px bad #FF7D8C, a 3px bad left bar runs the full panel height, and the error state component fills the body. Offline with cached content: unchanged, plus a Held banner above it — stale numbers are still numbers.
items.behaviour: Enters at 200ms/enter curve, opacity 0→1 with a 4dp rise. Children stagger 40ms to a maximum of six; beyond six they arrive together, because a staggered list of twelve reads as a stutter. No blur, no saveLayer, no BackdropFilter.
items.modes: Night has the outline and the declared rim and no shadow. Day has the outline and sh1 and no rim. Veld has a 2px border and nothing else.
items.accessibility: Semantics container:true with an explicit label naming the cluster ('Territory instrument cluster'), so a screen reader announces the group before its cells. The outline is a real 3:1 edge, not a decorative rim, so the panel boundary survives greyscale and sun. At 2.0× the panel is height-intrinsic and its internal 2×2 cell grid collapses to 1×4 on a LayoutBuilder width threshold, never on a scale guess.
items.amber: none. The panel is a container and containers are never lit. It declares no TorchClaim.
items.screenshot: A slightly-lighter navy rectangle on near-black with a soft 14dp corner, a thin cool grey outline and a single pale line along its top inside edge, divided across its middle by one thin horizontal rule that runs edge to edge.

items.name: Plate
items.purpose: The photographic surface — the one hard-edged, full-bleed element in the system, and the only object allowed to carry a strip light.
items.anatomy: 21:9 full-bleed band, radius 20 (r20) when inset, 0 when bled to the screen edge. The image is baked server-side by sharp: desaturated to 12% chroma, luminance-crushed so no pixel exceeds plate-ceiling #474747, and the radial edge-dissolve written into the PNG's own alpha channel at device width. The client draws one Image with cacheWidth = devicePixelRatio × logicalWidth. Over it, WHEN TorchClaim.plateStripLight IS GRANTED: one strip light — a 2px #FFB162 line with a LinearGradient bloom above it (#FFF1DE@0.55 → #FFB162@0.30 → transparent, 48dp tall), clamped out of the lower 40% of the plate. Under any text block, a bottom-up LinearGradient scrim abyss-000 0%→80%, 96dp tall, always, granted or not. Text hangs off the left gutter (20/40), never centred: eyebrow 11/700 ink-2, then the figure on its own baseline, then one body line.
items.states: LOADED, LIT — the strip light renders. LOADED, UNLIT — TorchScope denied the claim, which happens on any tabbed Night route that also carries a primary commit action (agent outlet detail with 'Check in here' is the real case, and I am naming it rather than pretending the ladder never bites). The plate keeps its image, its scrim and its type; it simply does not carry a light. This is the Day treatment applied in Night, and it is already specified, already tested and already legible. Loading: the well fill at the exact 21:9 geometry with a 1px edge-structure outline round the band and one 1px edge-control rule where the scrim's top edge will land — no shimmer, no amber. Ineligible (a detected face, another manager's territory, a fraud flag, or a failed luma-variance check): falls through to Plate fallback. Fallback: five horizontal rules receding in perspective on abyss-000 at a FIXED perspective series — REVISED, the data claim is deleted. The first draft varied their spacing by the territory's OSA trend and called that 'generated from data, never a placeholder'. The critic is right that nobody can decode line spacing into an availability trend, that two territories produce two abstract patterns a manager cannot tell apart, and that a screen-reader user gets nothing: it was decoration wearing a data alibi, which is worse than decoration. The rules are now a constant texture, and the fact the plate was carrying renders ON the fallback as one sentence at body ink-1 with its figure in JBM — 'On-shelf availability down 6 points this month' — with a matching semanticLabel. If the rules are granted amber they render at 0.30 → 0.04 as one drawn object; if denied they render in edge-structure. Error (image 404 or decode failure): the fallback, silently. Collapsed: a 96dp band, user preference, shipping on day one. Offline with no cached bytes: the fallback.
items.behaviour: Reveal at 320ms/enter — opacity 0→1 plus, where granted, the strip-light gradient's own stops animating 0→full over the same window, which reads as a light coming on. Where denied, the reveal is opacity alone. One AnimationController, disposed on route exit. No ShaderMask, no ImageFiltered, no saveLayer: a ShaderMask over a 1080×463 band is a 3–6ms offscreen allocation re-rastered every frame of the reveal, which is the whole frame budget.
items.modes: Night only. In Day the plate renders at 44% of the fold with no strip light and no scrim; the text block moves below the image. In Veld the plate does not render at all — it is replaced by the outlet name at title.l and the one fact the plate was illustrating. An agent in the sun cannot see a photograph and does not need one.
items.accessibility: Image carries a server-supplied semanticLabel naming the outlet and the capture date, never 'shelf photo'. The worst case the type can encounter is measured: ink-1 on the scrim over a full-value strip light is 10.56:1, the eyebrow 7.15:1, and ink-1 on the icon-disc worst case (abyss-000@70% over the #474747 ceiling, flattened to #1D2025) is 13.5:1 — the server-enforced ceiling is what makes every one of those computable rather than a hope. At 2.0× the text cluster is a Wrap, so the delta drops to its own line and the scrim grows with it.
items.amber: declares TorchClaim.plateStripLight, precedence 2. Granted: one object — the strip light, the archetype of the law, a depicted light source rather than a label. Denied: none, and the plate is still a plate.
items.screenshot: A wide near-monochrome photograph of a shop shelf, crushed almost to silhouette, with a single warm horizontal line of light across its upper third glowing softly upward, and the outlet name and a large number sitting bottom-left over a darkened wash.

items.name: Soft row
items.purpose: The list primitive the whole app is built from: a full-width soft surface in three densities.
items.anatomy:
Three densities, one component. COMPACT min-height 56, padding 12 vertical / 20 horizontal, internal gap 12 (s3) — Console lists. STANDARD min-height 64, padding 16/20, gap 16 (s4) — Field lists, the ladder, stop rows. TALL min-height 80, padding 16/20 — rows with a second meta line: Next-up, outbox, person rows.
Structure left to right: optional 3px severity left bar, full row height, flush to the leading edge; optional 28–44dp leading glyph or thumb; a title/subtitle column taking all remaining width; optional trailing figure (JBM figure.s) or a 20dp chevron in ink-3.
FILL AND EDGE — REVISED, and this is the second blocker. Night: fill abyss-100 #141D27, radius 14, AND a 1px edge-structure #5A7088 outline on every row. The first draft carried no border and claimed 'identity is geometry, not fill: rows are separated by an 8dp gap'. That is circular and I should have caught it: an 8dp gap of ground between two rows is only perceivable if the rows are perceivable, and #141D27 on #0B1017 measures 1.12:1 — weaker even than the 1.21 I quoted. On a 6-bit panel at 40% backlight in a back aisle the list was floating text with no row boundary and no tap affordance. THE CORRECTED CLAIM: the edge identifies the row, the gap groups the rows. Both do work; only one of them can be the identifier.
I considered and rejected raising the fill instead: a Night fill reaching 3:1 on ground lands around #4A5B70, which is a button, not a row, and it would turn the darkness from the site into a backdrop. A 1px edge-structure line at 3.73:1 is a quiet line — it is not the 'hard box' owner decision 2 rules out, the radius-14 silhouette and the borderless Day treatment carry that decision, and physics does not negotiate.
Day: fill #FAF7F2, radius 14, sh1, NO outline — on a light ground the shadow is the edge and it works. Where a Console list must be gapless, the fill drops to transparent and a 1px hairline-decorative divider carries the separation.
items.states: Default. Pressed: fill → lifted #2C3B4D, scale 0.98, 120ms/state, Buzz.tick. Selected: outline thickens to 1px edge-control plus a 3px ink-1 left bar plus title at body.strong — three channels, no colour. Disabled: fill unchanged, ink → ink-mute, chevron removed, no press feedback, and a meta line naming why (a dead row with no explanation is a phone call to a manager). Loading: skeleton at the same geometry, inside the same outline. Empty: the list renders the Empty state, never a zero-height row. Error: 3px bad left bar, subtitle replaced by the failure in body ink-1 with a filled triangle, trailing chevron replaced by a Retry tertiary. SLOW DATA — REVISED: the previous values stay at FULL contrast and a Held square plus the word 'updating' renders in the meta line. The first draft dimmed the row to 0.6 opacity, which is a state the CI contrast walk cannot see and which made an already-quiet row quieter at the moment it was least trustworthy. Offline: unchanged, plus a Held flag chip in the meta line. Severity: critical = 3px solid bad-solid left bar; watch = a 3px bad OUTLINE bar (a 1px bad stroke round a transparent 3px channel), not the same bar at 40% opacity — same reason. On-target and neutral: no bar.
items.behaviour: Whole row is the tap target — never a small trailing button, because a thumb in a shop aims at the row. Long-press opens the row's overflow sheet where one exists, with Buzz.tick. Rows are const-constructible; the outline is a single Border on the row's existing BoxDecoration, which costs nothing a fill did not already cost, and there is still no blur, no shadow and no gradient inside any ListView.builder row.
items.modes: Night: well fill, 1px edge-structure outline, 8dp gaps. Day: card fill, sh1, no outline, 8dp gaps. Veld: white fill, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border, 12dp (s3) gaps, min-height 64 at every density — the three densities collapse to one, because Veld halves density by rule.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true, label: '<title>. <subtitle>. <severity word>') with severity announced FIRST on worklist rows. Tap target is the full row, always ≥48 (≥56 Veld). At 2.0× the row is intrinsic-height, the title wraps to three lines then ellipsises, the trailing figure drops beneath the subtitle rather than squeezing the title, and the chevron stays vertically centred on the first title line, not on the row.
items.amber: none, and it declares no TorchClaim. A list row is never lit — this is the rule that kills the amber-dot-on-every-row failure, and the Person row below is now held to it too.
items.screenshot: A stack of full-width soft dark rectangles floating on a blacker ground, each outlined in a thin cool grey line with clear gaps between them; each holds a bold name, a quieter line of reason beneath, and a right-aligned monospaced number; one row carries a short vertical crimson bar hard against its left edge.

items.name: Section state glyph
items.purpose: The four-state capture marker used on every ladder row, in the submit gate and on the outcome breakdown — including the fourth state, 'can't confirm'.
items.anatomy: 28dp square tile, radius 6 (r6), 2px border in edge-control, joined to the tiles above and below by a 2px vertical rule in hairline-decorative so nine of them read as a ladder you climb. Four fills: EMPTY — transparent, border only, nothing inside. HALF — the lower half filled in ink-2, a hard horizontal stop at the tile's centre. DONE — solid good #6FE0AE (Night) / #14664A (Day) / #0F5039 (Veld) with a 2px ground-coloured tick. CAN'T CONFIRM — 45° hatch, hard-stop LinearGradient stripes 3dp on, 3dp off, in chart-neutral #8B8271, with a 2px horizontal bar across the tile's middle. The hatch is the encoding; there is no fourth hue. Alongside, in the row, the state's word at label 13/500 ink-2: 'Not started', 'In progress', 'Done', "Can't confirm".
items.states: The four above, plus: REQUIRED-AND-EMPTY — the empty tile's border thickens to 2px ink-1 and the row gains a REQUIRED flag chip; the tile never turns red, because a section you have not reached is not a failure. PRESSED — tile scales 0.94 while the row scales 0.98, 120ms. DISABLED (a section locked until check-in) — border ink-mute, a 2px diagonal strike across the tile, and a meta line naming the unlock condition.
items.behaviour: State transitions are instant fills, no cross-fade — an agent glancing at a ladder needs the current truth, not a 200ms lie. Reaching DONE fires Buzz.tick; reaching CAN'T CONFIRM fires nothing, because it is not an achievement. The connecting rule between two DONE tiles fills to good, giving the ladder a visibly climbed lower half.
items.modes: Night as specified. Day swaps good and ink tokens to the light column; the hatch swaps to ink-3 #676052. Veld: 32dp tile, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border, DONE is a solid #0F5039 block with a white tick, HALF is a solid #1B2632 lower half, hatch stripes thicken to 4dp on / 4dp off in #4A4437 — thin hatch disappears in glare.
items.accessibility: Four distinct silhouettes — nothing, a half-block, a tick, a hatch-with-bar — so the state survives greyscale, deuteranopia and a sun-washed panel. Semantics label is the state word plus the section name: "Pricing, can't confirm". The word always renders next to the glyph; the glyph is never alone. At 2.0× the tile stays 28dp (it is a graphic, not text) while the row grows around it and the connecting rule stretches.
items.amber: none, in any state. No TorchClaim. Capture progress is status, and status never gets the torch.
items.screenshot: A vertical chain of nine small rounded squares linked by a thin line: the top four are solid green with ticks, the fifth is half-filled, the sixth is filled with fine diagonal stripes and a bar through it, and the last three are empty outlines — with a section name and a state word beside each.

items.name: Person row
items.purpose: Replaces every screen that currently prints a raw database id with a human: name, role, outlet.
items.anatomy: Soft row, TALL density (min-height 80, padding 16/20), with the Night 1px edge-structure outline. Leading: a 44dp avatar — a radius-10 thumbnail where a photo exists, otherwise a radius-10 well-filled tile with a 1px edge-structure outline carrying the person's initials at figure.s in ink-2, never a generic silhouette icon. Title: full name at title.m ink-1. Meta: role at label 13/500 ink-2, a 3dp ink-3 middot, then the outlet or territory at label ink-2, middle-truncated so the branch survives ('Shoprite Kli…Mall'). Trailing: optional figure.s, a chevron, or a Live indicator. The database id is NEVER rendered; where support needs it, long-press → 'Copy agent id' copies it in mono.ident.
items.states: Default. Unknown person: initials tile shows a 2px-stroke question glyph, the title reads 'Unknown user' at ink-2, and the meta line shows the id in mono.ident — the one place the raw id is legitimate, because it is now the only fact. Deactivated: ink drops to ink-mute, a 'Deactivated' flag chip replaces the role, no chevron, not tappable. Loading: 44dp outlined well square plus a 140×16 and a 200×12 block. Offline: a cached person renders normally; an uncached person shows the unknown treatment rather than a spinner that will never resolve. You: the name is followed by ' · you' at meta ink-3 — never a coloured badge. LIVE (an agent mid-visit) — REVISED, and the critic is exactly right. The first draft gave every live row a pulsing amber dot 'counting as one object', which on a Tuesday morning is eleven pulsing dots down a fourteen-agent list: the amber-dot-on-every-row failure, reintroduced one component after the soft row killed it, plus eleven unboundaried per-frame repaints in a scrolling list. THE RULE NOW, borrowed from the outbox row which had it right: at most ONE pulsing dot per list, on the first live row in view, and it is a TorchClaim that must be granted. Every other live row — and every live row at all when the claim is denied — renders a static 8dp filled square in ink-2 plus the word 'Live'. Each dot sits in its own RepaintBoundary.
items.behaviour: Tap opens the person's detail where one exists; otherwise the row drops its chevron and is not interactive, rather than becoming a dead tap. Avatar images decode with cacheWidth 88. Long-press copies the id and raises a toast, Buzz.tick.
items.modes: Night/Day per the soft row. Day and Veld never pulse amber — abyss-400 / #1B2632 plus the word, as the direction requires. Veld: 56dp initials tile, 2px border, name 18/600, role and outlet stacked on two lines rather than middot-joined, because a joined line at 16/600 in glare is one long smear.
items.accessibility: Semantics label is 'name, role, outlet' as one sentence, with 'deactivated', 'you' or 'live' appended. Initials tiles carry the full name as their label, not the initials. The pulse degrades to the static square plus the word under reduce-motion, which is the same thing every denied row already renders — so the reduce-motion path is exercised on every list, every day. At 2.0× the middot join breaks into two stacked lines via a Wrap, which is also what Afrikaans at p90 1.40× needs.
items.amber: declares TorchClaim.livePulse, precedence 5, at most one instance per route, Night only. Denied or reduce-motion: a static ink-2 square plus the word 'Live'.
items.screenshot: A soft dark outlined row with a small rounded square showing two pale initials, a name in medium weight beside it, and beneath that a quieter line reading 'Field agent · Kasi Corner Spaza'; at its right a small grey square and the word 'Live'.

items.name: Live outbox row
items.purpose: Makes the sync queue a place rather than a rumour: one queued item, its live state, its size, and a way in.
items.anatomy: Soft row, TALL density, with the Night outline. Leading: a 28dp radius-6 state tile matching the section-state glyph's geometry, carrying a per-state silhouette. Title: what the item is, in title.m — 'Shelf photo · Kasi Corner Spaza'. Meta line one: the state sentence in label ink-2. Meta line two: size and age in meta ink-3, size in JBM — '1,4 MB · queued 14:03'. Trailing: a 20dp chevron. When sending, a 2px progress bar inset to the row's content box, flush to the row's bottom inner edge, radius 0.
items.states: QUEUED — square glyph, Oatmeal on the well, 1px edge-control; sentence 'Waiting for signal'. This is the normal state of South African field connectivity and it is never styled as an error. SENDING — the glyph becomes a filled square with the 2px progress bar beneath showing real bytes, not a fake sweep; sentence 'Sending now'; the pulse is a TorchClaim, at most one per route, on the row at the head of the queue, and denied rows show the filled square without motion. RETRYING — a clock silhouette; 'Retrying at 14:20' with the actual next-attempt time in JBM, never 'will retry soon'. STUCK — 3px bad left bar, filled triangle glyph, the real SyncProblem: 'The server said no (422)', 'Signed out — sign in to send', 'Too big to send as it is'; chevron becomes a Fix tertiary. SENT — the row leaves the list on a 200ms exit; it does not linger as a green tick. WAITING FOR VISIT — a chain-link silhouette, 'Waits for the visit above it', not tappable, because tapping it can do nothing. OFFLINE entirely — every row QUEUED, Offline banner above. PAUSED — hollow square, 'Paused to save data · send now'.
items.behaviour: The row is tappable in every state except WAITING FOR VISIT: tapping opens the item's detail, where the captured work is visible — the point is that held work can always be seen. The retry clock counts down in real minutes from the outbox's own schedule; it never invents one. Byte progress updates at most 4×/second. Rows reorder only on a state change, never on a progress tick, and reorder with a 200ms move.
items.modes: Night: one pulsing amber square at the head of the queue when granted. Day and Veld: an abyss-400 / #1B2632 pulse plus the word 'Live', because a pulsing amber dot on a light ground would spend the screen's one amber on a progress indicator. Veld: 2px bordered white row, state word at 17/600, progress bar 4px solid #1B2632 on a white track with a 2px border.
items.accessibility: Semantics(liveRegion: true) on the state sentence only — the sentence changes, the row does not re-announce wholesale. Label: '<state>. <what>. <size>. <age>.' with state first. Every state has its own silhouette and sentence; colour appears only on STUCK and only as a left bar accompanied by a triangle and a word. At 2.0× both meta lines wrap and the row grows past 80 freely; the progress bar stays 2px.
items.amber: declares TorchClaim.livePulse, precedence 5, one instance, Night only, and only while something is genuinely sending. Thirty queued rows with three sending show one pulse.
items.screenshot: A soft dark outlined row with a small square marker, the words 'Shelf photo · Kasi Corner Spaza', beneath it 'Retrying at 14:20' and '1,4 MB · queued 14:03' in a monospaced grey, and a chevron at the right.

items.name: Primary button
items.purpose: The one commit action on a screen — the thing the agent or manager came to do.
items.anatomy: Height 56 Field / 44 Console / 64 Veld, full width by default, radius 10 (r10), label at label 13/500 (Field 15/600, Veld 15/600 minimum), optional 18dp 2px-stroke leading icon with an 8dp gap. Night, GRANTED: fill lifted #2C3B4D, 1px #FFB162 rim (6.37:1 on its own fill, 10.65:1 on ground), ink Palladian #EEE9DF (9.43:1), plus a 2dp amber gradient bleed along the top inside edge (#FFF1DE@0.55 → #FFB162@0.30 → transparent) — the button is lit from above, not painted. Day: fill Burning Flame #FFB162, ink #1B2632 (8.55:1). Veld: fill #FFB162, ink veld-ink #0E141A (10.34:1), radius 0, 2px #0E141A border.
items.states: DEFAULT as above. DENIED (Night only, and only where a route's declared `subject` promoted another claim above it — in practice the Ask answer route): fill lifted, 1px edge-control rim, ink-1 label, no bleed. It remains visually the heaviest control on the screen by fill and position; it simply is not lit. PRESSED: fill → flame-500 #F79742 with the ink STAYING DARK (#0B1017 on #F79742 = 8.59:1; the flame-900-on-flame-500 pressed state from the first draft was 2.00:1 and erased the label at the moment of commitment), plus scale 0.98 at 120ms/state, plus Buzz.tick. BUSY: label replaced by three 6dp Oatmeal dots on a 600ms loop, the button keeps its exact width so nothing reflows, taps swallowed, semantic label becomes '<label>, sending'. Never a spinner. DISABLED: fill well, ink ink-mute, 1px edge-control outline retained so the control is still a control, no rim, no bleed, no press feedback — and a BarNote directly beneath at meta 12/400 ink-3 naming exactly what blocks it ('Stock counts and pricing still to capture'). That BarNote is a hard requirement, not an option: a disabled primary without a reason is a dead end in a shop. BECOMES-ENABLED: fill and rim ease in over 200ms/enter rather than snapping. OFFLINE: unchanged — it commits to the outbox and the toast says 'Held on this phone'; it is never disabled for want of signal. ERROR ON COMMIT: returns to default, a toast carries the reason, the button is immediately pressable again.
items.behaviour: One per route, registered with the route as its primary commit widget — TorchScope reads that registration and the narrowed lint reads it too. Sits in the thumb zone (a 96dp bottom region with a 1px hairline above it), never in a header. Double-tap debounced at 400ms. On success the button does not celebrate; the screen moves.
items.modes: Night is a dark block lit along its top edge with an amber rim. Day and Veld are a solid amber block with dark ink. This inversion is the direction: on a dark ground amber is light; on a light ground amber is a thing you press.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true, enabled:, label:) always; the label is the verb phrase, never 'OK'. At 2.0× the label wraps to two lines and the button grows to intrinsic height with 16dp vertical padding — never pinned to 56, never ellipsised, because a commit action you cannot read is not a commit action. Afrikaans at p90 1.40× is the case this was sized for.
items.amber: declares TorchClaim.primaryCommit, precedence 1 — the top of the ladder in every skin. On a Night tabbed route it takes the single content grant; on an untabbed route (inside a visit, in a sheet) it takes one of two.
items.screenshot: A wide dark slab with softly rounded corners, a thin warm line tracing its top edge and glowing faintly downward into the fill, with 'Check in here' centred in warm off-white.

items.name: Secondary button
items.purpose: The credible alternative — 'Start over', 'Search by name', 'Skip this outlet'.
items.anatomy: Ghost. Transparent fill, 1px edge-control (#7C93AC Night, 6.02:1 on ground / #6E6657 Day), ink-1 label at the same metrics and heights as the primary (56 / 44 / 64), radius 10. Optional 18dp 2px-stroke leading icon in ink-1.
items.states: Default. Pressed: fill → press-ghost-night #18212D (the declared flattened hex, not an alpha multiplier) / #E2DBCC in Day, border unchanged, scale 0.98, 120ms, Buzz.tick. Disabled: border → ink-mute, ink → ink-mute, plus a BarNote. Busy: three 6dp ink-2 dots on the 600ms loop. Loading (the action's target is still loading): the button renders enabled and its tap opens the destination's own loading state — a secondary is never disabled for a reason the user cannot see.
items.behaviour: Never more than one secondary beside a primary; a third option becomes a tertiary or moves into an overflow sheet. In a two-button row the primary takes 60% of the width and sits on the right; in a two-button column (the Field default) the primary sits on top and the secondary beneath with a 12dp gap, because the thumb reaches the bottom of the screen first and the bottom-most control must not be the destructive one.
items.modes: Night: cool blue-grey 1px border on black. Day: warm 1px border on paper. Veld: white fill, 2px #1B2632 border, ink #0E141A, radius 0, height 64 — in Veld the secondary and the primary differ only by fill (white vs amber), which is enough at 18.52:1 and 10.34:1 plus their label verbs.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true). At 2.0× it wraps and grows exactly as the primary does. It carries no colour signal at all, so there is nothing to lose in greyscale.
items.amber: none, ever. No TorchClaim. A secondary that goes amber steals the commit action's identity.
items.screenshot: A wide transparent slab outlined in a thin cool grey line, holding 'Start over' in warm off-white, sitting directly under a lit amber-rimmed button.

items.name: Tertiary button
items.purpose: An inline action inside a row, a sheet or an error — 'Retry', 'Fix', 'Copy id', 'Undo'.
items.anatomy: Text only. Label at label 13/500 (Veld 16/600) in ink-1, with a 2px underline in edge-control 3dp below the baseline — the underline is what makes it read as an action without a border or a colour. Tap target padded to 48×48 minimum (Veld 56×56) with EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 12, vertical: 14) even though the ink occupies less. Optional 16dp 2px-stroke leading icon, 6dp gap.
items.states: Default. Pressed: underline thickens to 3px and the label goes to weight 700, 120ms; no fill, no scale (a text button that scales looks broken). Disabled: ink-mute, underline removed — with the underline gone it stops reading as an action, which is correct. Busy: the label is replaced by three 4dp dots on the 600ms loop at the same measured width. Destructive variant: ink → bad (#FF7D8C / #8C1B2C), underline → bad, and a 12dp filled triangle precedes the label. Loading: never shown as a skeleton — a tertiary appears only when its action is available.
items.behaviour: Used at most twice in any one container. Inside a soft row it sits at the trailing edge and steals the tap from the row (the row's own tap is suppressed within a 12dp halo). Buzz.tick on press.
items.modes: Night and Day are identical in structure. Veld: label 16/600, underline 3px #0E141A, tap target 56, and the destructive variant becomes ink #7A0F22 with a 3px underline.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true) with an explicit label; 'Retry' alone is forbidden where two retries can appear on one screen — it is 'Retry sending the shelf photo'. The underline means the action does not depend on colour to be found. At 2.0× it wraps within its container and its tap target grows with it.
items.amber: none. No TorchClaim.
items.screenshot: The word 'Retry' in warm off-white with a short thin rule beneath it, sitting at the right-hand end of a dark row.

items.name: Destructive button
items.purpose: Discarding captured work — 'Start over', 'Discard this visit', 'Remove competitor'.
items.anatomy: Never the primary geometry. Full width, height 56 / 44 / 64, radius 10, transparent fill, 2px bad #FF7D8C border, ink bad, a 16dp filled triangle before the label, label at label 13/500 weight 600. The SOLID crimson form (bad-solid #E23C55 Night with ground ink at 4.55:1 for its large label / #7A0F22 Day and Veld with white ink at 10.94:1) is reserved for the confirming button inside a decision sheet — the second, deliberate press.
items.states: Default (outlined). Pressed: fill → wash-bad-night #302933, the declared flattened hex rather than a 12% alpha — decoration only, since the 2px border, the triangle and the scale carry the press. Scale 0.98, 120ms, Buzz.warning (heavier than tick). Confirming (inside the sheet): solid fill, and its pressed state darkens by one ramp step while the ink stays fixed. Busy: three 6dp dots in bad. Disabled: border and ink ink-mute, triangle outlined not filled, plus a BarNote. Guarded: where the work being destroyed is unsent, the label carries the count — 'Discard 12 held captures' — and the button will not render without that count resolved; if the count is still loading, the button is busy, not enabled.
items.behaviour: A destructive action ALWAYS opens a decision sheet; it never acts on first press. It is never the bottom-most control in a thumb-zone column. The sheet's dismiss is non-destructive. Buzz.warning on the first press, Buzz.success on completion of the safe path, nothing on completion of the destructive path — a destroyed thing does not get a congratulation.
items.modes: Night: crimson outline on black. Day: darker crimson outline on paper. Veld: 2px #7A0F22 border, ink #7A0F22 at 10.94:1, radius 0, height 64, and the confirming form is a solid #7A0F22 block with white ink.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true, label: '<verb>, <what is lost>'). The filled triangle is a shape, not decoration — the state is legible in greyscale. Never relies on crimson: the triangle and the verb carry it. At 2.0× the label wraps and the triangle stays aligned to the first line.
items.amber: none, categorically. No TorchClaim. There is no amber warning in TradeIQ.
items.screenshot: A wide transparent slab outlined in a 2px muted-rose line, with a small solid triangle and the words 'Discard 12 held captures' in the same rose.

items.name: Icon button
items.purpose: A single-glyph control — back, close, overflow, torch, skin cycle — with a label that cannot be omitted.
items.anatomy: 48dp square (Field 48, Console 44, Veld 56), 24dp 2px-stroke glyph in ink-1, transparent fill, no border, radius 10 for the press surface. Over a photograph or a plate it gains a 32dp abyss-000@70% disc — solid, never a blur. Because the plate's server-enforced ceiling is #474747, the worst case that disc can flatten to is plate-disc-worst #1D2025, on which ink-1 measures 13.5:1; over an arbitrary un-ceilinged image the disc would be unmeasurable, which is precisely why the ceiling is enforced server-side.
items.states: Default. Pressed: a press-ghost-night #18212D disc appears behind the glyph and the glyph scales 0.94, 120ms, Buzz.tick. Disabled: glyph ink-mute, no press surface. Toggled-on (torch, skin, filter): the container becomes a filled block — Night lifted #2C3B4D with a 1px edge-control rim (NOT an amber rim: torch-on as an amber block was the pun that gave the agent three amber meanings back to back, and the rim version is the same pun at 1px), Day and Veld a solid Abyssal #1B2632 block with an amber glyph and, where space allows, the word ON at 11/700. Badged: an 8dp ink-1 disc at the glyph's top-right with the count in JBM 10/600 inside when ≤9, a plain disc above that. Loading: skeleton 24dp square, outlined.
items.behaviour: semanticLabel is a REQUIRED constructor argument — the widget will not compile without it, which is how the audit's 26 unlabelled IconButtons cannot recur. Long-press raises a tooltip with the same string.
items.modes: Night: pale glyph on black. Day: dark glyph on paper. Veld: 56dp target, 26dp glyph at 3px stroke, toggled-on is a solid #1B2632 block with a white glyph and the word ON at 16/600 — no rim, because rims do not survive glare.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true, toggled: <bool where applicable>, label:). Toggle state is announced, not inferred from the glyph. Tap target never below 48 (56 Veld) regardless of glyph size. At 2.0× the glyph does not scale (it is a graphic) but the target grows to 56 so it keeps pace with the text around it.
items.amber: none in any skin — REVISED. The first draft allowed a 1px amber rim on a toggled-on control 'counting against the budget'. It declares no TorchClaim now: toggled-on is a filled block plus a word, everywhere. A toggle state is a label, and amber is never a label.
items.screenshot: A small warm-white outline glyph of a sun in a 48dp square at the left of a thumb-zone bar; when active it sits inside a solid slightly-lighter block with a thin cool rim and the word ON.

items.name: Text field
items.purpose: Free text — a note, an outlet search, a skip reason, a competitor name.
items.anatomy: A trough. Label ABOVE at label 13/500 ink-2 — never a floating placeholder, because a floating label destroys the field's own name the moment you type in it. 8dp gap. The trough: fill well #141D27 / #E2DBCC, radius 10 at the BOTTOM corners and 0 at the top (a trough holds at the bottom), 1px edge-control rule along the bottom AND a 1px edge-control outline up the sides and across the top in Night — REVISED, because a trough identified only by a #141D27-on-#0B1017 fill and one bottom rule is a floating line on black; the outline is quieter than the bottom rule at the same token and gives the field a body. Min-height 56 Field / 44 Console, padding 14 horizontal / 16 vertical, text at body 15/400 ink-1. Below, 6dp gap, optional help at meta 12/400 ink-3. Multi-line grows from 3 lines to 8 then scrolls internally with the bottom rule staying put.
items.states: EMPTY: a hint at body ink-3 restating the unit or format ('e.g. 12 facings'), never repeating the label. FOCUSED: bottom rule becomes 2px flame-700 #FFCB94 (10.38:1 on surface) with a 6dp downward gradient bloom; caret in flame-700; 120ms. FILLED: rule back to 1px edge-control. ERROR: bottom rule 2px bad, message beneath at 12/500 bad with a 12dp filled triangle, and the message replaces the help line rather than pushing it. DISABLED: fill L0 ground, rule and outline ink-mute, ink ink-mute, plus a help line saying why. READ-ONLY: no rule, no outline, no trough fill, ink-1 text — it stops looking like a field. CHARACTER LIMIT: a JBM counter at meta appears at 80% of the cap, right-aligned under the trough, turning to bad ink at 100% — never a hard silent truncation. OVER-LONG INPUT: the trough scrolls horizontally on a single-line field; the value is never clipped without a scroll affordance. LOADING: skeleton trough at the exact geometry with the label already rendered. OFFLINE: unchanged.
items.behaviour: Keyboard type and capitalisation declared per use. The trough scrolls into view above the keyboard with a 16dp margin at 200ms. The soft keyboard's action key moves to the next field, never commits the form. Autocorrect off for anything resembling an identifier.
items.modes: Night: a sunken near-black outlined trough, found by its body and its heavier bottom rule. Day: a sunken warm well on paper. Veld: white fill, 2px #1B2632 border on all four sides, radius 0, height 64, text 17/600; focus is a 3px #0E141A outer offset ring at 3dp offset instead of a glow, because glows do not exist in Veld.
items.accessibility: The visible label IS the semantic label (Semantics + TextField label, not a hint). Errors use Semantics(liveRegion: true). The error is a triangle plus a sentence plus a rule, three channels. At 2.0× the label, the input text and the help all scale, the trough becomes intrinsic-height, and a two-field row breaks to a column on a LayoutBuilder threshold.
items.amber: the focus rule and its bloom — exempt from TorchScope by declaration, because exactly one field can hold focus, the ring is transient, and it renders only under keyboard, switch-access or D-pad navigation. The exemption is written into TorchScope rather than left as prose.
items.screenshot: A label in muted warm grey above a slightly-sunken dark rectangle outlined in a faint cool line with a heavier line along its bottom edge; when active that bottom line thickens into warm amber and bleeds a short soft glow downward.

items.name: Numeric field
items.purpose: A typed figure where a stepper is wrong — a price, a large count, a percentage.
items.anatomy: The text field's trough, with four differences. The value renders in JetBrains Mono figure.m 22/600 tabular, right-aligned, because a column of prices must align on the decimal. A unit or currency prefix/suffix sits in label 13/500 ink-3 inside the trough, outside the tap-to-edit area. The trough is 120dp wide minimum when it sits in a row of two. Keyboard is numeric with a decimal point matching the locale's separator — an Afrikaans user gets a comma.
items.states: EMPTY: an em dash in ink-3, not a zero and not a hint. Load-bearing: not counted and counted-as-zero are different facts. ZERO: '0' in ink-1, rendered, never suppressed. ZERO-AS-FINDING: the trough takes a 2px bad rule and outline, a wash-bad-night #302933 fill as declared decoration, and a 'Finding' status chip beneath; Buzz.finding on landing there. NEGATIVE: a true minus sign, never a bracket. FOCUSED / ERROR / DISABLED / READ-ONLY: as the text field. OUT OF RANGE: rule 2px bad with 'Between 0 and 9 999' beneath; the value is not silently clamped. LOCALE MISMATCH: '1.5' typed in an Afrikaans locale is accepted and normalised on blur with the normalised value shown — never rejected. PROVISIONAL: where the figure came from the server but the phone has a newer local value, the trough shows the local value and a meta line reads 'scored 71, you saw 84' with both figures in JBM. OVERFLOW — REVISED, the critic is right and the failure he describes is a wrong number confirmed by a manager who read the field back. A right-aligned 22/600 JBM value of 'R 1 234 567,89' is roughly 145px in a 92dp usable trough, and inheriting the text field's scroll-from-the-left behaviour hides the leading digits and displays '4 567,89'. Numeric troughs now anchor the LEADING digits on overflow and scroll the trailing ones, a 12dp ground-to-transparent fade marks the trailing edge as partial, and while the field holds focus the full value renders beneath the trough at figure.s in JBM. A figure is never partially displayed without a mark that it is partial.
items.behaviour: All formatting runs through one locale-driven NumberFormat, replacing the hardcoded en_US formatter in rich_figures.dart. On focus the whole value is selected, so typing replaces rather than appends — with one deliberate exception, the count stepper's inline field, for the reason given there. On blur the value is formatted; while focused it is raw.
items.modes: Night / Day per the text field. Veld: 64 tall, 2px border, value at JBM 24/600, unit at 16/600, and the zero-as-finding state becomes a 3px #7A0F22 left bar plus the words 'Out of stock' — a wash is invisible in sun.
items.accessibility: Semantics value is spoken as a number with its unit ('twelve facings'), not as digits. The em dash announces as 'not counted'. Zero-as-finding announces as 'zero, out of stock, a finding'. The overflow state appends 'value continues' so a screen-reader user is told the display is partial. At 2.0× a two-field row breaks to a column; the value never shrinks to fit.
items.amber: none. Focus ring only, exempt.
items.screenshot: A narrow sunken dark trough with 'R' in small grey at its left and '1 234 567,' in a monospaced figure running to a soft fade at its right edge, with the full value repeated small beneath it.

items.name: Count stepper
items.purpose: Counting stock one-handed while the other hand is on the shelf.
items.anatomy: REVISED GEOMETRY — the critic found the control inverted and he is right: minus and plus were 56dp each and the keyboard-opening centre was about 190dp, so the biggest target was the rarest action and hitting it covered the screen. A single 56dp-high (Field) unit, radius 10, fill well, 1px edge-control border, divided by 1px hairlines into FOUR zones: a 72dp minus tile, a flexible INERT centre (~132dp at 360dp), a 44dp pencil tile, a 72dp plus tile. Step tiles carry 24dp 2px-stroke glyphs in ink-1; the pencil tile carries a 20dp 2px-stroke pencil in ink-2, visibly quieter so it does not compete. The centre shows the value in JetBrains Mono figure.m 22/600 tabular, centred, and is NOT a tap target — the keyboard is behind the pencil, which is explicit, small and discoverable, where the first draft's long-press-only alternative would have been neither.
items.states: NOT COUNTED (null): centre shows an em dash in ink-3. From here, minus means 'there are none' and records an explicit 0; plus means 'I counted one' and records 1, never 0 — landing on zero by accident would silently raise a task for a manager. COUNTED: value in ink-1. ZERO AS FINDING (zeroIsFinding): the entire control takes the finding treatment — wash-bad-night #302933 fill, 2px bad border, value in bad, an 'Out of stock' status chip beneath; the whole control changes, not just the digit, so it reads from arm's length in a dark aisle. AT MIN: minus tile disabled, glyph ink-mute, no haptic. AT MAX: plus tile disabled likewise. PRESSED (any tile): tile fill → lifted, glyph scale 0.9, 120ms. EDITING: the centre becomes a numeric field and the ± and pencil tiles stay visible but disabled so the control does not change shape. Critically, and unlike every other numeric field in this kit, THE CARET LANDS AT THE END AND NOTHING IS SELECTED — a stray press on the pencil must never be able to replace a count with one digit, which was the real data loss in the critic's scenario. An 'Undo' tertiary replaces the help line for 5 seconds after any edit; tapping outside restores the prior value unchanged. DISABLED (section locked): whole control at ink-mute with a diagonal 2px strike across the centre and a reason line beneath. LOADING: skeleton at the exact 56dp geometry, outlined. OFFLINE: unchanged — counting has never needed a network.
items.behaviour: Haptics are the point: Buzz.tick on every ordinary step, Buzz.finding — a heavier, distinct double — on landing at zero when zeroIsFinding, because the agent is looking at the shelf and needs to feel the count land. Buzz.tick plus a tooltip ('Type a count') on the pencil. Hold-to-repeat: after 500ms, steps repeat at 8/second, with the haptic dropping to every fifth step so a long hold does not become a buzz. The value animates with AnimatedCount at 120ms; at high repeat rates the animation drops to an instant set. The control scrolls itself 16dp above the keyboard on edit so the ladder behind it is never what the keyboard covers.
items.modes: Night: sunken dark control, pale glyphs, amber nowhere. Day: warm well, dark glyphs. Veld: 72dp high, 96dp step tiles, 56dp pencil tile, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 borders including between the four zones, value at JBM 28/600, and the finding state becomes a solid #7A0F22 left block 8dp wide plus the words 'OUT OF STOCK' at 16/700 beneath.
items.accessibility: Semantics(value: '<n> facings', increasedValue:, decreasedValue:) so a screen reader user gets the adjustable role and can step it with a gesture. The ± tiles carry 'One fewer' / 'One more' naming the unit; the pencil carries 'Type a count'. The finding state announces 'zero, out of stock, this raises a task'. At 2.0× the control grows to 72dp and the centre figure scales; the ± tiles keep their widths and grow in height with the row.
items.amber: none in any state. No TorchClaim. A stock count is data, and data is never lit.
items.screenshot: A wide sunken dark capsule split by hairlines into a broad minus at the left, a large monospaced '12' in the middle, a small quiet pencil, and a broad plus at the right — or, when the count is zero, the whole capsule washed faintly rose with a 2px rose edge and 'Out of stock' beneath it.

items.name: Toggle
items.purpose: A binary fact captured on the shelf — 'Planogram compliant', 'Fridge working'.
items.anatomy: A row: label at body 15/400 ink-1 taking all available width, then a 12dp gap, then the track. Track 52×32, radius 16, thumb 26dp circle with a 3dp inset. OFF: track fill well, 1px edge-control border, thumb in ink-3, thumb at the left. ON: track fill good #6FE0AE (Night) / #14664A (Day), no border, thumb in ground colour, thumb at the right, and a 2px tick drawn inside the thumb. The tick is what makes the state survive greyscale. Row min-height 64 (Field), the whole row is the target.
items.states: Off. On. Pressed: thumb scales to 28dp, 120ms/state, Buzz.tick. Disabled: track ink-mute fill, thumb ink-mute, label ink-mute, plus a reason line at meta. INDETERMINATE / NOT ANSWERED is not a toggle state — an unanswered binary is a Choice row with two options and no selection, because a toggle sitting at 'off' is a recorded 'no', and silence is not 'no'. Any toggle whose value can be unknown must be built as a choice row instead, and the widget asserts this in debug. Loading: skeleton 52×32 block plus a label block. Error (the write failed): the toggle returns to its previous position on a 200ms exit curve and a toast names the failure — it never sits in a state the server rejected. Offline: commits locally, no visual difference.
items.behaviour: Tap anywhere on the row. The thumb travels at 120ms/state; the track's colour crosses at the same time so there is never a green track with a left-hand thumb. Drag is supported but not required.
items.modes: Night: dark track, mint fill when on. Day: warm well track, deep green fill when on. Veld: track 64×36 with a 2px #1B2632 border in BOTH states, thumb 30dp, ON fills the track solid #0F5039 with a white thumb carrying a #0F5039 tick, OFF leaves the track white with a #1B2632 thumb — and the words ON / OFF render at 16/700 immediately right of the track, because at 56dp targets in glare a thumb position alone is a coin toss.
items.accessibility: Semantics(toggled: <bool>, label: <the fact, not the control>). The tick inside the thumb plus the thumb's position are two non-colour channels; Veld adds the word as a third. At 2.0× the label wraps to as many lines as it needs, the row grows, and the track stays 52×32 pinned to the first line of the label.
items.amber: none. No TorchClaim.
items.screenshot: A row reading 'Fridge working' in warm off-white with a small dark capsule at the far right; flipped on, the capsule is mint green with a pale circle at its right carrying a tiny dark tick.

items.name: Checkbox
items.purpose: Multi-select inside a section — visibility elements present, materials deployed.
items.anatomy: 24dp square, radius 6 (r6), 2px edge-control border, transparent fill. CHECKED: fill good, border good, a 2.5px ground-coloured tick inset 5dp. THE MIXED STATE IS DELETED — REVISED, and the critic caught a real internal contradiction: a mixed state was fully specified for 'a parent over partly-checked children' while the same item said group select-all is a tertiary button above the group and never a fourth checkbox state. No parent checkbox exists anywhere in the 60 screens, so mixed was a token, a painter branch, a golden, a semantics case and a line in the contrast test that nothing could ever reach. It goes. If the visibility section later genuinely needs parent-over-children, it comes back with the screen that uses it. Sits in a row: 24dp box, 16dp gap, label at body 15/400 ink-1, row min-height 56 (Field 64), whole row tappable.
items.states: Unchecked. Checked. Pressed: box scales 0.9 and a 40dp press-ghost-night disc appears behind it, 120ms, Buzz.tick. Disabled: border and fill ink-mute, label ink-mute, plus a reason line. Error (a required group with nothing checked, after a submit attempt): the GROUP takes a 2px bad left bar and a message beneath with a filled triangle; individual boxes do not turn red, because no single box is wrong. Loading: skeleton 24dp square plus a label block. READ-ONLY (reviewing a submitted visit) — REVISED: boxes render checked/unchecked with no border and no press surface, and the label drops to ink-2. The first draft used 0.8 opacity, which is a state the contrast walk cannot see; I am banning it for testability, not because 0.8 failed AA.
items.behaviour: Tap target is the row. Rapid multi-select does not re-animate: after three ticks within 600ms the tick draw drops to an instant set. Group select-all is a tertiary button above the group.
items.modes: Night: cool outline, mint fill when checked. Day: warm outline, deep green fill. Veld: 32dp box, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border, checked = solid #1B2632 fill with a 3px white tick (not green — in Veld, filled-vs-empty is the signal and #0F5039 is reserved for success blocks), row height 64.
items.accessibility: Semantics(checked:, label:) on the row. The tick and the fill are two channels; the box is never signalled by colour alone. At 2.0× the label wraps, the row grows, the box stays 24dp and top-aligns to the first line rather than centring on a four-line label.
items.amber: none. No TorchClaim.
items.screenshot: A short list of rows, each with a small rounded square at the left; the checked ones are filled mint with a crisp dark tick, the unchecked ones empty with a thin cool outline.

items.name: Choice row
items.purpose: One answer from two to four options, shown all at once — the shape most of the capture sections actually need.
items.anatomy: Options in a Row with 8dp gaps, each Expanded to an equal share. Each option: height 48 Field / 44 Console, radius 10, transparent fill, 1px edge-control border, label at label 13/500 ink-2 centred. SELECTED: fill lifted #2C3B4D, border 1px ink-1, label at weight 700 in ink-1, and a 6dp filled circle at the option's leading edge with an 8dp gap. Three channels: fill, weight, and a mark.
items.states: NOTHING SELECTED — the legitimate default, visually distinct from any selection: all options at rest, and where the group is required, a meta line beneath reads 'Not answered yet'. This is the state a toggle cannot express and is why choice rows exist for uncertain binaries. Selected. Pressed: option scales 0.98, 120ms, Buzz.tick. Disabled option: ink-mute, border ink-mute, a 2px diagonal strike, and a meta line naming why. All disabled: the group renders read-only. Error after submit: the group takes a 2px bad left bar and a triangle-prefixed message; no individual option turns red. Loading: skeleton pills at the same geometry. Too many options: above four, or where any label exceeds 14 characters, the component switches from a Row to a Column of full-width 56dp rows with the mark at the leading edge — automatically, on an intrinsic-width measurement, not on a guess.
items.behaviour: Selecting is immediate and local; there is no confirm. Re-tapping a selected option does NOT deselect — clearing an answer is a tertiary 'Clear' beneath the group, because an accidental deselect in a shop loses a fact silently.
items.modes: Night: outlined pills, the selected one a filled slightly-lighter block. Day: the same in the light column. Veld: always the Column form regardless of option count, 64dp rows, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 borders, selected = solid #1B2632 fill with a white 17/600 label and a white filled circle. Veld never renders a horizontal choice row — three side-by-side 56dp targets in the sun is a mis-tap.
items.accessibility: Semantics(inMutuallyExclusiveGroup: true, selected:, label:) per option, with the group carrying a label naming the question. The filled circle plus the weight shift carry selection without colour. At 2.0× the component switches to the Column form on the same intrinsic-width measurement that handles long labels, and Afrikaans at 1.40× triggers it naturally rather than truncating.
items.amber: none. No TorchClaim. A selection is not a light source; this is the component the direction's chip rules protect most often.
items.screenshot: Three equal outlined pills reading 'Yes', 'No', "Can't tell" — with 'No' filled a shade lighter, its label bolder, and a small solid dot at its left edge.

items.name: Filter chip
items.purpose: Narrowing a list — territory, date window, status. Manager surfaces mostly, agent My-work secondarily.
items.anatomy: Outlined, transparent, 1px edge-control, radius 6 (r6), height 44 Console / 48 Field / 56 Veld, padding 12 horizontal, label at label 13/500 ink-2. Optional 16dp 2px-stroke leading glyph, 6dp gap. A chip carrying a count shows it in JBM figure.s after the label with an 8dp gap. Chips live on a horizontally scrolling rail with a 20dp leading gutter, 8dp between chips, and a 20dp trailing gutter so the last chip is never flush to the edge.
items.states: Default. SELECTED: fill lifted #2C3B4D, border 1px ink-1 (NOT amber — the direction's original selected-chip border was amber and would multiply across a rail), label weight 700 ink-1, and a 14dp 2px-stroke tick before the label. Three channels. PRESSED: scale 0.98, 120ms, selection click haptic. DISABLED (a filter with no possible results): ink-mute, border ink-mute, count shows 0, and the chip stays visible — hiding a filter because it is empty hides the fact that it is empty. LOADING: the chip renders with its label and a 24×14 outlined skeleton block where the count will be, at exactly the width the count will occupy so the rail does not reflow. ALL-CLEAR: when nothing is selected, a leading 'All' chip renders selected; there is never a rail with no selection. OVERFLOW: chips never wrap — the rail scrolls, and a 24dp right-edge fade to ground signals more. In Veld the rail does not scroll: it becomes a two-column grid of full-width chips, because horizontal scroll discovery fails outdoors. ERROR — REVISED: the rail keeps the last good selection at FULL contrast and the error state renders below the rail, not in it. The first draft dimmed the rail to 0.6, which hid the cause at the moment the user needed to see it, and which the contrast walk could not test.
items.behaviour: Selecting applies immediately with no Apply button. Multi-select rails show selected chips in place, never reordered to the front — reordering under a thumb is a mis-tap. Rail position is preserved across rebuilds.
items.modes: Night: cool outlines on black, selected chip a lighter filled block. Day: warm outlines on paper. Veld: 56dp, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 borders, selected = solid #1B2632 with a white 16/700 label and a white tick.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true, selected:, label: '<filter>, <count> results'). The tick plus the weight plus the fill give three non-colour channels. At 2.0× chips grow to intrinsic height and wrap their labels to two lines, and the rail's height grows with them; labels never ellipsise, because a truncated filter name is a filter you cannot identify.
items.amber: none. No TorchClaim.
items.screenshot: A horizontal row of small outlined capsules reading 'All', 'Gauteng North 14', 'Needs a decision 5' — with the second one filled a shade lighter, carrying a small tick and bolder text.

items.name: Status chip
items.purpose: The current standing of the thing it sits on: Critical, Watch, On target, Held, Live.
items.anatomy: Radius 6, height 28 inline (32 Field, 40 Veld), padding 10 horizontal, label at 11/700 in sentence case (uppercase at 11px in glare fills counters), 6dp gap to a leading 12dp silhouette. Five declared levels, each with hue, silhouette and word bound in ONE token so they cannot drift apart: CRITICAL — solid bad-solid fill (#E23C55 Night with ground ink / #7A0F22 Day and Veld with white ink), filled triangle, word 'Critical'; the owning row also takes a 3px left bar. WATCH — transparent fill, 1px bad border, bad ink (6.94:1 on well), half-filled triangle, word 'Watch'. ON TARGET — transparent, 1px good border, good ink (10.49:1 on well), filled circle, word 'On target'. HELD — well fill, 1px edge-control, ink-2, filled square, word 'Held' — deliberately not a severity, because queued work is the normal state of South African field connectivity. LIVE — well fill, 1px edge-control, ink-2, an 8dp dot, word 'Live'.
items.states: The five levels above. Pressed (where the chip is tappable to an explanation): scale 0.98, 120ms. Not tappable: no press feedback at all, so a chip that does nothing does not invite a tap. Unknown / not yet computed: the chip does NOT render — an em dash renders in its place at ink-3 with 'not scored' in meta. A grey 'Unknown' chip is a claim that the system looked; the em dash is the truth. STALE — REVISED, and this is the one the critic priced exactly: a 'Watch' chip at 0.6 opacity in Night computes to 3.29:1 for 11px text, below the 4.5:1 floor CI claims to enforce, and CI passed because it tested the undimmed pair. The dim is deleted outright rather than replaced. Staleness is a WORD: the chip renders at full level treatment and the age renders beneath it at meta ink-3 — 'Watch · as at 08:15'. A timestamp is more precise than a fade and it is the thing the agent actually needs. Reduce-motion: the Live dot becomes a filled square plus the word, no pulse.
items.behaviour: At most one status chip per row. A row that would carry two statuses carries the more severe one and moves the other into its detail. Chips never animate in.
items.modes: Night: crimson and mint on near-black, held in Oatmeal on the well. Day: the darker crimson and green columns on paper. Veld: 40dp high, radius 0, 2px borders, CRITICAL a solid #7A0F22 block with white 16/700 ink, WATCH a 2px #7A0F22 outline with #7A0F22 ink, ON TARGET a 2px #0F5039 outline, HELD a 2px #4A4437 outline — every one at or above 9.66:1.
items.accessibility: The semanticLabel is the level's declared word and ships in the same token as the hue and the glyph, so a level cannot be added without one. Worklist rows announce the status first. Four distinct silhouettes — filled triangle, half triangle, circle, square — plus five distinct words, so the level survives greyscale, both dichromacies and a washed-out panel. At 2.0× the chip grows to intrinsic height and wraps; the glyph stays 12dp and aligns to the first line.
items.amber: NONE at any level in any skin. The Live dot declares TorchClaim.livePulse, precedence 5, Night only, one per route; denied or in Day/Veld it is an abyss-400 dot plus the word. A static amber chip is the exact failure the amber law exists to prevent.
items.screenshot: A small solid rose block with a white triangle and the word 'Critical'; beside it a transparent capsule outlined in rose with a half-filled triangle and 'Watch'; beside that a neutral capsule with a small square and 'Held'.

items.name: Flag chip family
items.purpose: Facts about how a piece of work was produced — out of fence, flagged for review, unfinished visit, skipped, held — which are not severities and must never be coloured as though they were.
items.anatomy:
One component, one treatment, six members. Radius 6, height 28 inline / 32 Field / 40 Veld, padding 10 horizontal, fill well, 1px edge-control border, label at 11/700 ink-2, leading 14dp 2px-stroke glyph in ink-2 with a 6dp gap. The family is identified by its uniform neutral treatment; the members by glyph and word:
• OUT OF FENCE — a broken-ring glyph, word 'Out of fence', measured distance appended in JBM: 'Out of fence · 140 m'.
• FLAGGED FOR REVIEW — an eye-with-a-bar glyph, word 'For review'.
• UNFINISHED VISIT — a three-quarter ring with an open arc, word 'Unfinished', fraction in JBM: 'Unfinished · 6/9'.
• SKIPPED — a struck ring, word 'Skipped', plus the chosen reason.
• HELD — a filled square, word 'Held', plus the count.
• NO GPS — a hollow pin with a gap, word 'No GPS'.
Chips wrap in a Wrap with 8dp main and cross spacing; they never scroll.
items.states: Default. Pressed (every flag chip is tappable to its explanation — a flag the agent cannot interrogate is an accusation): scale 0.98, 120ms, opens a sheet naming what the flag means, what produced it, and what happens next. CLEARED — REVISED: ink drops to ink-3 #A79E8C (6.41:1 on well, a declared token), a 1.5px strike runs through the label, and the word 'Cleared' is appended, for one session, then it stops rendering. The first draft used 0.6 opacity, which the contrast walk cannot see. Multiple flags: up to two render; a third becomes a '+2' chip in the same treatment opening a sheet listing all of them. LOADING — REVISED, and the critic found a real contradiction: the kit forbids a bottom sheet from resizing under a thumb and then let every row in a scrolling list grow by a 32dp chip band after first paint, so a row reaching a descending thumb shifts and the wrong outlet gets tapped. THE RULE NOW: locally-derived flags — out of fence, unfinished, no GPS, held — are synchronous and render on the FIRST FRAME, always. Where a server-derived flag is pending, the row RESERVES the band's height from first paint as empty space — no skeleton block, so nothing is claimed — and the chip reveals in place at 200ms without moving anything. Where no flag is possible, no band is reserved. Offline: local flags render normally; server-derived flags do not render at all rather than render stale, and their reserved band is released on the first frame because the outbox already knows there is no network.
items.behaviour: A flag never changes the colour of its own chip by severity. Where a flag carries a real consequence, the CONSEQUENCE is expressed on the owning row's 3px severity left bar and in the row's reason line, not in the chip. This is the rule that keeps the flag family readable: one treatment, six meanings, escalation held elsewhere.
items.modes: Night: neutral Oatmeal-on-well chips. Day: the same in the light column. Veld: 40dp, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border, label 16/700 #0E141A, glyph at 3px stroke — and only ONE flag chip renders inline, with any others behind a '+n'. Veld halves density by rule and a wrap of four chips is half a screen.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true, label: '<word>, <detail>, tap to find out why'). Six distinct silhouettes carry the members apart with no colour difference at all between them — which is the point, and which means the family is fully legible in greyscale by construction. At 2.0× chips grow and wrap freely; the Wrap absorbs Afrikaans expansion without any measurement.
items.amber: none, categorically, in every skin. No TorchClaim. A flag is a label, and amber is never a label.
items.screenshot: Two small neutral capsules under a visit row: one with a broken-circle glyph reading 'Out of fence · 140 m', one with a three-quarter arc reading 'Unfinished · 6/9' — both the same quiet grey, neither red.

items.name: Skip-reason picker
items.purpose: Recording why an outlet on the route was not visited, so a skip becomes data instead of a hole.
items.anatomy: A bottom sheet, Field density. Grabber 40×4 in grabber-night #616465 (declared hex, not an alpha), 16dp top padding. Title at title.l 20/600: 'Why are you skipping Kasi Corner Spaza?'. Body at body ink-2: 'This goes to your manager with the route.' 24dp gap. A Column choice row — four full-width 64dp options, 8dp gaps, each with a leading mark position and a label at body 15/400: 'Store refused', 'Not stocked here', 'Equipment broken', 'Something else'. Choosing 'Something else' reveals a text field beneath at 200ms labelled 'What happened?' with a 200-character counter; the sheet scrolls to keep it above the keyboard. Thumb zone: a 1px hairline, 16dp padding, a BarNote, the primary 'Skip this outlet' at 56dp, and a secondary 'Keep it on my route' beneath at a 12dp gap.
items.states: NOTHING CHOSEN — the primary is disabled and the BarNote reads 'Choose a reason first'. This is the default and the sheet opens in it. CHOSEN — the primary enables over 200ms/enter. SOMETHING-ELSE WITH AN EMPTY NOTE — the primary stays disabled, BarNote 'Say what happened'; the note is required precisely because 'other' with no text is the hole this component exists to close. SUBMITTING — primary busy with the three-dot loop. OFFLINE — commits to the outbox; the toast says 'Skip held on this phone'; the primary is never disabled for signal. ERROR — the sheet stays open, the primary returns to default, and a bad-bordered message renders above the thumb zone naming the failure. DISMISSED — nothing is recorded, the outlet stays on the route; dismissal is always the safe path. ALREADY SKIPPED — the previous reason renders selected, the title becomes 'Change why you skipped…', the primary reads 'Update reason'. NO REASONS CONFIGURED — the four defaults render, because a skip must always be recordable; a meta line notes 'Using the standard reasons'.
items.behaviour: Opened from the stop row's overflow, never from a swipe — a swipe-to-skip in a moving taxi is an accidental skip. Buzz.tick on selecting a reason, Buzz.warning on commit, because a skip removes work from the day. On commit the sheet closes at 320ms/exit and the stop row collapses to a skipped state carrying the Skipped flag chip with the chosen reason appended.
items.modes: Night: abyss-200 sheet with an edge-structure outline. Day: #FAF7F2 sheet with sh3. Veld: white sheet, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border, 72dp option rows, labels at 17/600, primary 64dp amber block with #0E141A ink, secondary a 2px-bordered white block.
items.accessibility: The sheet is a Semantics route with a header label; focus lands on the title. Options are in a mutually-exclusive group. The disabled primary's BarNote is a liveRegion, so a screen reader user hears why it will not fire without hunting for it. At 2.0× the four options grow to intrinsic height, the sheet becomes scrollable with the thumb zone pinned below the scroll, and nothing in the thumb zone is ever scrolled off.
