items.amber: declares TorchClaim.primaryCommit. A sheet is an untabbed route, so it holds 2 grants in Night and 1 in Day/Veld, and the commit block is the only claimant — the sheet's whole allowance, deliberately unspent beyond it.
items.screenshot: A sheet risen from the bottom of a black screen with a short pale grabber, a bold question, four stacked outlined rows of which 'Store refused' is filled and marked, and at the foot a lit button reading 'Skip this outlet' above a ghost button reading 'Keep it on my route'.

items.name: Floating pill navigation
items.purpose: The app's top-level movement — a floating bar above the content, not welded to the bottom edge.
items.anatomy:
A pill floating 20dp above the safe-area bottom, inset 16dp left and right, height 64, radius r-pill (999, reinstated by owner decision 3). Fill #141D27 FULLY OPAQUE with a 1px edge-structure #5A7088 outline (3.73:1 on ground) — there is zero BackdropFilter anywhere in the application, and no scroll-listener swaps the fill, because mutating the layer tree on the two frames a user perceives most sharply makes the bar visibly change colour whenever anyone touches a list. Contents: FOUR SLOTS MAXIMUM — REVISED, the fifth Menu slot is gone as a fifth and becomes the fourth where a role needs it (manager: Dashboard, Ask, Work, Menu). The critic's arithmetic is the reason: at 360dp the bar is 360 − 32 insets − 12 gap − 64 circle = 252dp, so five slots are 50dp each, under 48 plus any gutter once the active pill's 6dp inset is drawn. Four slots are 63dp. Each slot: a 24dp 2px-stroke glyph with a label at 11/700 beneath at a 4dp gap. The circle action sits to the pill's right with a 12dp gap, outside the pill.
ACTIVE TAB: a solid amber pill inset 6dp within the bar — height 48, radius 999, fill #FFB162, glyph and label in ground #0B1017 at 10.65:1, label weight 700 against inactive 500.
items.states: Default with exactly one active slot. Pressed (inactive slot): glyph scales 0.9 and a 48dp press-ghost disc appears behind it, 120ms, selection haptic. Active slot re-tapped: scrolls that tab's list to the top; a second re-tap within 2s refreshes it. Badged: an 8dp ink-1 disc at a glyph's top-right with a JBM count inside at ≤9, a plain disc above; badges are never amber and never crimson — the count is the signal. Disabled slot (a tab the role cannot reach): the slot does not render; the bar redistributes to three. Offline: unchanged. The nav never reflects connectivity. Hidden: absent entirely inside a visit — agents get tabs on their home screen only, because mid-visit navigation loses captured work. Keyboard open: translates off-screen at 200ms/exit, returns at 200ms/enter. LABELS — REVISED. The first draft dropped labels below a 360dp breakpoint and claimed they 'wrap to two lines' at 2.0×, neither of which survives Afrikaans, where the failure is a single unbreakable word in a fixed slot: 'Kompetisies' at 11/700 is about 67px against a 63dp slot, and at the 1.3× text scale common on cheap Androids every label overflows. The bar now MEASURES: at build, a TextPainter lays out every localised label at the current textScaler against the computed slot width, and if any one overflows the whole bar goes icon-only — all four, never a mixed bar. Labels never ellipsise and never wrap in the nav. Icon-only keeps the tooltip and the full Semantics label.
items.behaviour: The bar and the circle sit in a Row inside a SafeArea with a 20dp bottom margin; content padding reserves 64 + 20 + safe area so nothing scrolls under nothing. Tab switches are instant — no cross-fade between tab bodies. The amber pill does NOT slide between slots: it is drawn in place at the new slot, because a sliding amber pill across a nav bar is the single most recognisable borrowed gesture in the reference set.
items.modes: NIGHT: the active tab is the solid #FFB162 pill with #0B1017 ink, and it holds TorchScope's reserved CHROME grant whenever the nav renders. DAY and VELD: the active tab is a solid lifted #2C3B4D block with Palladian ink at 9.43:1 (Veld: solid #1B2632 with white ink at 15.33:1, height 72, labels always render, white fill, 2px #1B2632 border, pill geometry kept because shape is load-bearing identity and geometry costs nothing in glare) — NOT amber, because Day and Veld allow exactly one amber block per screen and that block belongs to the screen's primary commit action.
items.accessibility: Each slot is Semantics(button: true, selected:, label: '<tab name>, tab <n> of <m>'). The active state carries fill plus weight plus, whenever labels render, the word — and the pill's fill is a 10.65:1 shape rather than the 1.5–2.0:1 tint the reference used. At 2.0× the measurement above will almost always have gone icon-only, where the fill and the tooltip carry the state; the bar's own height grows to 88dp when labels do render at scale.
items.amber: ONE in Night, held as TorchScope's reserved chrome grant — and here I depart from the critic, who wants the tab to yield to the primary per route. I will not make the app's permanent furniture change colour as you move between tabs; that reads as a rendering bug, not as a law. Night's rule is instead learnable in a sentence: the torch is in your hand and on the shelf, one each — chrome takes one grant, content takes the other, and content therefore has exactly one amber object on any tabbed route and two where the nav is absent. ZERO in Day and Veld.
items.screenshot: A dark capsule floating clear of the bottom of the screen with four small glyph-and-label pairs, the second of them sitting inside a solid warm amber lozenge with near-black ink; a separate dark circle with a pale arrow floats to its right.

items.name: Nav circle action
items.purpose: The role's one standing action, always in the thumb's reach: a manager raises a task or assigns a visit; an agent starts an unplanned visit.
items.anatomy:
A 64dp circle beside the nav pill, 12dp gap, vertically centred on it, radius 999. Contents: a 26dp 2px-stroke glyph, centred, nothing else. A label at 11/700 ink-2 may sit beneath the circle outside it for a role's first three sessions, then retires.
EXPECTED AND GRANTED: Night fill #FFB162 with a #0B1017 glyph; Day fill #FFB162 with a #1B2632 glyph; Veld fill #FFB162 with a #0E141A glyph and a 2px #0E141A border. EXPECTED AND DENIED, or NOT EXPECTED: Night fill lifted #2C3B4D with a 1px edge-control rim and an ink-1 glyph; Day fill #FAF7F2 with sh2 and an ink-1 glyph; Veld white with a 2px #1B2632 border and a #0E141A glyph.
items.states: Expected. Not expected. Pressed: scale 0.94 and, when amber, fill → flame-500 #F79742 with the glyph staying dark at 8.59:1, 120ms, Buzz.tick. Busy: the glyph is replaced by three 5dp dots on the 600ms loop, the circle keeps its size. Disabled (the role has the action but not right now — an agent with no GPS fix): fill well, 1px edge-control outline, glyph ink-mute, no press, and a tap raises a toast naming the blocker rather than doing nothing. Hidden: inside a visit, and on any route with no standing action; the nav pill then takes the full inset width. Badged: an 8dp ink-1 disc at the top-right when the action has a pending count. Offline: fully available — an unplanned visit and a raised task both start locally.
items.behaviour: Becoming expected is a 200ms/enter transition, never a pulse — a pulsing amber circle would claim something is happening right now, which is reserved for the live state. Long-press opens the action's variants where it has any (assign a visit vs raise a task) in a bottom sheet, and on a manager nav it is also where the retired fifth tab now lives.
items.modes: In Night an amber circle is emitted light beside a lit tab pill. In Day and Veld it is the screen's one amber block, which is why the Day nav-active tab is an ink block rather than an amber one.
items.accessibility: Semantics(button: true, label: '<the verb phrase>') — 'Start a visit here', never 'Add'. Expected vs not-expected is NOT carried by colour: the glyph changes from an outlined plus to a filled arrow when expected, and the label beneath (or the tooltip) changes wording — which is exactly what makes the denied path harmless. At 2.0× the circle stays 64dp — it is a target, not text — and any label beneath wraps.
items.amber: declares TorchClaim.navCircle, precedence 4, and it is ADMISSIBLE ONLY ON A ROUTE WITH NO PRIMARY COMMIT ACTION — REVISED. The critic's scenario is the one that broke the first draft: an agent standing at an outlet on Today, circle expected AND a 'Check in here' primary, which is two amber blocks on a light ground and three in Night. Two 'do this' claims on one screen is not a budget problem, it is a meaning problem, and the ladder resolves it structurally rather than by counting.
items.screenshot: A solid warm amber disc about the height of the nav bar beside it, holding a single near-black filled arrow, floating clear of the screen's bottom edge.

items.name: App header
items.purpose: Names where you are and offers at most one action — without AppBar chrome.
items.anatomy: No Material AppBar, no elevation, no background change on scroll. A 96dp region (Console 72) on the ground colour, gutter-aligned. Line one: optional 48dp back icon button at the leading edge, inset −12dp so the glyph optically aligns to the gutter. Line two: the title at title.l 20/600 (Field 24/600). Line three: the subtitle at label 13/500 ink-2, a single line of facts joined by 3dp middots — 'Spaza · Tembisa Ext 12 · 1,2 km · last visit 12 Aug'. Trailing: at most one icon button, vertically centred on the title line. Below: 24dp before content, and no divider — the gap is the separation, and a header sitting on the ground needs no edge because it is text on ground, not a surface.
items.states: Default. Scrolled: the title does NOT shrink, move or collapse; the header scrolls away like content. A collapsing header animates on every scroll frame and costs the exact budget the plate needs. Where a persistent title is required, a 44dp compact bar fades in at 200ms carrying the title at title.m, opaque well fill, 1px hairline beneath. With a plate: the header's text sits over the plate's scrim and the back button gains its 32dp disc. Loading: title is a 200×20 outlined skeleton block, subtitle a 260×13 block, back button renders normally. Error (the entity failed to load): the title falls back to the route's generic name ('Visit'), the subtitle carries the failure at ink-2 with a Retry tertiary. Offline: the subtitle appends '· offline copy' at meta ink-3 when the facts shown are cached.
items.behaviour: Back is a real pop, never a route replacement. Where captured work would be lost, back opens the decision sheet instead. Mid-visit there is no back at all — the header shows the outlet and the exit is an explicit control in the thumb zone.
items.modes: Night: pale title on near-black, no chrome. Day: dark title on paper. Veld: title at 22/600, subtitle broken from middot-joined into two stacked lines at 17/600, back button 56dp, and a 2px #1B2632 rule beneath the header because in Veld a gap is not enough separation at 40dp block spacing.
items.accessibility: Semantics(header: true) on the title so a screen reader can jump to it; the subtitle is a separate node read as a sentence, not as middots. Back carries 'Back to <destination>', never 'Back'. At 2.0× the title wraps to three lines and the header grows past 96dp; the subtitle wraps freely via a Wrap that breaks the middot joins into stacked lines — which is also what Afrikaans p90 needs.
items.amber: none. No TorchClaim. The header is never the lit object on a screen.
items.screenshot: Near-black space with 'Kasi Corner Spaza' in large warm off-white hung off the left gutter, and beneath it a quieter grey line of facts separated by small dots — no bar, no line, no shadow.

items.name: Bottom sheet
items.purpose: The standard modal container — detail, overflow, picker, explanation.
items.anatomy: Radius 14 at the top two corners only, fill abyss-200 #1B2632, 1px edge-structure outline on the top and sides, a 40×4 grabber-night #616465 bar centred 8dp from the top (the only centred element in the system besides the capture shutter), 16dp content padding, gutter 20. Scrim abyss-000@72%, NO blur. Max height 92% of the screen; content scrolls inside while any thumb-zone action stays pinned beneath the scroll with a 1px hairline above it. Safe-area bottom padding added inside the sheet, not outside.
items.states: Default. Dragging: follows the finger 1:1; released below 40% of its height it dismisses at 320ms/exit, above it springs back at 320ms/enter. Scrolled to top and dragged down: dismisses rather than over-scrolls. Loading: the sheet opens immediately at its known height with a skeleton body — it never opens empty and grows, because a sheet that resizes under a thumb causes mis-taps. Unknown height: opens at 50% and does not resize; content scrolls. Empty: the empty state renders inside, left-aligned, at the sheet's natural height. Error: error state inside, sheet keeps its height. Offline: unchanged. Keyboard open: content scrolls to keep the focused field 16dp above the keyboard; the sheet itself does not resize. Stacked: a second sheet is forbidden — a sheet that needs a sheet replaces its own content with a 200ms slide and gains a back affordance at the leading edge of its title.
items.behaviour: Enters at 320ms/enter with the scrim fading over the same window. Dismiss on scrim tap, drag, and system back. A sheet holding unsaved input intercepts all three and opens the decision sheet instead. isScrollControlled always true.
items.modes: Night: a lighter navy sheet with a cool outline over a 72%-black scrim. Day: #FAF7F2 with sh3 and a scrim of rgba(27,38,50,.45). Veld: white sheet, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border on all visible sides, scrim rgba(14,20,26,.60), content padding 24, and no drag-to-dismiss — dismissal is an explicit 64dp 'Close' control, because a drag gesture with a gloved or sweating thumb in the sun is unreliable.
items.accessibility: Opens as a Semantics route with namesRoute and a header; focus moves to the title and is trapped until dismiss. The grabber carries 'Drag down to close'. At 2.0× the sheet's content scrolls and the pinned thumb-zone action grows to intrinsic height; the sheet's max height is unchanged, so the action is always reachable.
items.amber: none from the container. A sheet is an untabbed route: it opens its own TorchScope, and in practice its only claimant is its primary commit action.
items.screenshot: A panel risen from the bottom over a darkened screen, its top corners softly rounded, a short pale bar centred at its top edge, content hung off the left gutter and a single lit button at its foot.

items.name: Decision sheet
items.purpose: The gap-list component: when there is already captured work and the user is about to do something that touches it — carry on, or start over.
items.anatomy: A bottom sheet with a fixed anatomy that cannot be varied by the caller. Title at title.l: 'You have work here already'. Then a PROOF BLOCK — a well-filled radius-10 box with a 1px edge-structure outline, 16dp padding, listing what exists in concrete terms, each on its own line at body ink-1 with a leading 14dp section-state glyph: '6 of 9 sections captured', '3 photos held on this phone', 'Started 08:14, 41 minutes ago', figures in JBM. This block is the whole point: a decision about invisible work is a guess. Then 24dp. Then the actions as a column: PRIMARY 'Carry on where you left off' at 56dp; 12dp gap; DESTRUCTIVE-OUTLINED 'Start over' at 56dp with its filled triangle and, beneath it at meta ink-3, the exact cost — 'Loses 6 sections and 3 photos'. The safe action is on top, in the thumb's easiest reach; the destructive one is below it and is never the bottom-most control — a 48dp 'Close' tertiary sits beneath.
items.states: Default. Counting (the proof block's figures are still resolving): the sheet opens with the proof block in skeleton and BOTH actions busy-disabled, with a BarNote 'Checking what you have here' — neither choice may be made until the cost is known. Nothing to lose: the sheet does not open at all; the action proceeds. Confirming start-over: the destructive button becomes solid (bad-solid #E23C55 Night with ground ink, #7A0F22 with white ink Day and Veld), its label becomes 'Yes, start over' and a 3-second Undo toast follows. Offline: fully functional — every fact in the proof block is local. Error reading local work: 'Could not read what is on this phone' and ONLY 'Carry on' — it will never offer to destroy work it could not count. Session ended behind it: the sheet closes and the session-ended state takes the screen, carrying this same proof block.
items.behaviour: Opened by any navigation that would discard captured work: back from a visit, a re-check-in at an outlet with an open visit, a skip on an outlet already in progress. Buzz.warning on open. Never dismissible by scrim tap or drag — both map to 'Carry on', the safe path, but the sheet requires an explicit press so the choice is recorded. System back maps to 'Carry on'.
items.modes: Night / Day per the bottom sheet. Veld: white, 2px border, proof block a 2px-bordered white box with 17/600 lines, actions at 64dp, no drag, the destructive button a 2px #7A0F22 outline going to a solid #7A0F22 block with white ink on confirm.
items.accessibility: Route semantics with the title as header; focus lands on the proof block, not on a button, so the cost is read before the choice. Each action's label states its consequence in full ('Start over, loses 6 sections and 3 photos'). Nothing depends on colour: the safe action is identified by position, wording and the commit treatment; the destructive one by a triangle, a verb and a cost line. At 2.0× every line wraps, the sheet scrolls, and both actions grow to intrinsic height while staying pinned in order.
items.amber: declares TorchClaim.primaryCommit for 'Carry on' — the correct place for the torch, because it points at the safe path.
items.screenshot: A sheet reading 'You have work here already', below it an outlined box listing '6 of 9 sections captured' and '3 photos held on this phone' with small ladder glyphs, then a lit button 'Carry on where you left off' and beneath it a rose-outlined button 'Start over' with small grey text saying what that loses.

items.name: Dialog
items.purpose: A blocking question that is too small for a sheet and too important to dismiss — a session expiry, a permission rationale, a conflict.
items.anatomy: Centred horizontally, inset 32dp each side, max width 400dp, vertically centred but never taller than 80% of the screen. Fill abyss-200, radius 14, 1px edge-structure outline, 1px rim-night #303A43 top rim, 24dp padding. Title at title.l, 12dp gap, body at body 15/400 ink-2 with a maximum of four lines of copy, 24dp gap, actions as a column at 48dp each with 8dp gaps (never a right-aligned text-button row — a 48dp full-width dialog action is reachable and a 36dp text button in a corner is not). Scrim abyss-000@72%, no blur.
items.states: Default. Loading (waiting on the answer to the question it asked): actions busy, dialog does not close. Destructive: the confirming action takes the destructive button treatment and is second in the column. Non-dismissible (session expired, forced update): no scrim-tap dismiss, no system-back dismiss, only forward actions, and no X. Dismissible: scrim tap and back both map to the least destructive action. Error inside: the body is replaced with the failure and the actions collapse to one 'Close'. Offline: a dialog never asks a question it cannot answer offline; where the answer needs the network it renders its offline path ('This will send when you have signal') rather than blocking.
items.behaviour: Enters at 200ms/enter with opacity and a 0.96→1.0 scale — the one legitimate transient opacity in the kit, because it is a route transition and not a state. At most one dialog at a time; a second request queues. A dialog never carries a form — a form goes in a sheet, where the keyboard has room.
items.modes: Night: a lighter navy card floating over a darkened screen. Day: #FAF7F2 with sh3. Veld: white, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border, inset 24dp, padding 24, title 22/600, body 17/600, actions 64dp.
items.accessibility: Route semantics with namesRoute, alert role, focus trapped, focus lands on the title. Actions name their outcome. The dialog is announced in full on open. At 2.0× the body scrolls internally while the title and actions stay fixed, so the actions can never be pushed off-screen.
items.amber: declares TorchClaim.primaryCommit for its forward action, where it has one. A purely informational dialog ('Your session ended') declares nothing and its single action is a secondary.
items.screenshot: A small softly-rounded navy card floating in the middle of a darkened screen with a bold line of title, two lines of grey body, and two full-width stacked buttons beneath it.

items.name: Toast / snackbar
items.purpose: Confirming that something landed, or that it did not, without stealing the screen.
items.anatomy: Floats 20dp above the nav pill — or above the thumb zone where there is no nav — inset 16dp, radius 10, min-height 48, padding 12 vertical / 16 horizontal. Fill: NEUTRAL well #141D27 with a 1px edge-control border; SUCCESS wash-good-night #2A373D (the declared flattened hex, replacing the 12% alpha wash) with a 1px good border at 10.49:1 and a filled-circle glyph; FAILURE the well with a 2px bad left bar and a filled-triangle glyph. Leading 16dp glyph, 12dp gap, message at body 15/400 ink-1 over up to two lines, optional trailing tertiary action (Undo, View) with a 16dp gap.
items.states: Neutral. Success. Failure. With action: dwell extends from 3s to 6s, and the action's tap dismisses immediately. Queued: a second toast replaces the first at 200ms rather than stacking; a third within 2 seconds collapses both into a counted message ('3 captures held'). Persistent: a failure with an action that MUST be taken does not auto-dismiss — it stays until acted on or explicitly dismissed, and renders a 44dp close icon button. Offline confirmations: phrased as facts, not errors — 'Held on this phone · sends itself' — with the neutral treatment and a square glyph, never the failure treatment.
items.behaviour: Enters at 200ms/enter rising 8dp; exits at 200ms/exit. Dwell 3s neutral and success, 6s with an action, indefinite when persistent. Swipe right dismisses. A toast never covers the primary commit action: the thumb zone's height is added to its bottom offset. Buzz.success on a success toast, nothing on neutral, Buzz.warning on failure.
items.modes: Night: a dark floating bar with a thin edge. Day: #FAF7F2 with sh2. Veld: white, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border, message at 17/600, min-height 64, dwell doubled to 6s/10s — and success uses a solid #0F5039 block with white ink, failure a solid #7A0F22 block with white ink, because outlines and washes do not survive glare.
items.accessibility: Semantics(liveRegion: true) with the message; the action is a separate labelled button. Politeness is assertive for failures, polite for the rest. Three distinct glyph silhouettes carry the three kinds without colour. Dwell scales with the message's length (100ms per word above ten words) and, where the OS reports a reduced-motion or accessibility-timeout preference, all toasts become persistent with a close button.
items.amber: none. No TorchClaim. A toast is a report, and a report is never lit.
items.screenshot: A dark rounded bar floating just above the nav pill with a small circle glyph, the words 'Visit sent · scored 71' in warm off-white, and 'View' underlined at its right.

items.name: Loading skeleton
items.purpose: Holding the exact geometry of content that has not arrived, without lying about what it will be.
items.anatomy: REVISED, and this was a straight contradiction of my own device-floor rule. Night skeleton blocks were well #141D27 on ground #0B1017 — 1.12:1, exactly the ratio the foundations call unresolvable — so an agent on 3G watching My work load for four seconds saw a black screen with one sliding oatmeal line and assumed the app had broken. NOW: a skeleton that stands for a ROW or a PANEL is drawn as that object's real 1px edge-structure outline at its real geometry, empty — so the page is visibly a list of things arriving, and nothing moves when they do. A skeleton that stands for a TEXT LINE is a solid block filled edge-structure #5A7088 (3.33:1 on well, 3.73:1 on ground) at the text's line-height, radius 6, at the measured width of the real string: a title block at the title's width, a subtitle block at 60%, a trailing figure block at the figure's width. Day blocks stay well #E2DBCC, which works on paper. Never shimmer, never a gradient sweep.
items.states: BEFORE 600ms: nothing renders at all — the previous content stays, or the ground stays empty. Most loads finish inside 600ms and a skeleton that flashes is worse than a pause. AFTER 600ms: the blocks appear at 200ms/enter. AFTER 600ms AND STILL LOADING: a single 2px OATMEAL rule travels the top edge of the skeleton region left to right on a 1400ms linear loop. Oatmeal, not amber — a skeleton is loading, not live, and an amber pulse on a placeholder would tell a manager that a blank was real-time data. AFTER 10s: the travelling rule stops and a meta line appears beneath — 'Still fetching · this is slower than usual' with a Retry tertiary. AFTER 30s or on failure: replaced by the error state. PARTIAL: where some fields resolved, the resolved ones render real and only the unresolved ones are skeletons — a half-loaded row is honest. PAGINATION: the next page's skeletons render as exactly three rows at the list's foot, never a full screen.
items.behaviour: One shared Ticker subscriber drives the travelling rule for every visible skeleton, not one per block. The transition from skeleton to content is an instant swap with no cross-fade, because a cross-fade between a grey block and a number is a 200ms period of unreadable text.
items.modes: Night: outlined row shells with mid-grey text blocks inside them. Day: warm well blocks on paper. VELD: there is NO skeleton. A loading region in Veld renders the word 'Loading' at body.strong 17/600 in #4A4437 on the left gutter, and nothing else. Grey blocks on white in direct sun are invisible, and a moving rule is a distraction an agent on a shelf does not need.
items.accessibility: The skeleton region is Semantics(label: 'Loading <what>', liveRegion: false) and its blocks are excluded from the tree individually — a screen reader hears one 'Loading outlet list', not fourteen empty nodes. On arrival the region announces '<n> outlets'. Under reduce-motion or battery saver the travelling rule does not run; the static blocks and the 10s message carry it. At 2.0× the blocks scale with the text metrics they stand in for, so nothing jumps on arrival.
items.amber: none, ever, in any state. No TorchClaim. This is an explicit correction to the first draft of the direction, which put a pulsing amber on a skeleton.
items.screenshot: Three thin-outlined dark row shells where rows will be, each holding two mid-grey bars — a long one and a shorter one — with a single thin oatmeal line sliding slowly across the top of the group.

items.name: Empty state
items.purpose: Saying what to do next, in a place where there is nothing — never merely reporting the absence.
items.anatomy: LEFT-ALIGNED, never centred. Hung off the gutter, starting 40dp below whatever precedes it. A 64dp 2px-stroke line drawing in edge-control — and there are EXACTLY THREE, declared as a closed enum: SHELF (no content), PIN (no location), ENVELOPE (nothing sent). REVISED: the first draft said 'a single object drawn from the domain', which across at least eight named empty states means eight bespoke drawings nobody will commission, which means a stock outline set, which means the kit's most carefully argued anti-slop surface ends up wearing the same icons as every SaaS dashboard. A closed enum of three, reused by category, cannot drift — a fourth requires an owner decision and a drawing, not an import. 24dp gap. Headline at display 40/700 for a whole-screen empty, or title.l 20/600 in a panel — one short sentence. 8dp gap. One body line at body ink-2 naming the next physical action. 24dp gap. One secondary button, left-aligned at its intrinsic width.
items.states: NOTHING YET: SHELF. 'No outlets within 2 km. Search by name, or scan a shelf barcode.' — the action is physical and in the agent's world. ALL DONE: SHELF, but a different sentence and NO action button — 'Route done. 8 of 8 visited.' with the figures in JBM, because there is nothing to do. These two must never share a component instance; an empty route and a finished route are opposite facts. FILTERED TO NOTHING: SHELF. 'No outlets match Gauteng North + Critical.' with a 'Clear filters' secondary, and the filter rail stays visible above it at full contrast, because the cause must remain visible. SEARCH FOUND NOTHING: SHELF, and the query is echoed in mono.ident inside the body line so the agent can see the typo. PERMISSION MISSING: PIN, and the action is the permission request worded as what it buys — 'Turn on location to see outlets near you'. OFFLINE AND NOTHING CACHED: ENVELOPE. 'Nothing on this phone yet. It fills when you have signal.' with no retry button, because retrying without signal is theatre. Loading: the empty state does not render until loading resolves — an empty state during a load is a lie.
items.behaviour: Enters at 200ms/enter with a 4dp rise; its drawing does not animate. The secondary button is a real action with a real destination, never 'Refresh' where a pull-to-refresh already exists.
items.modes: Night: a cool line drawing and a large pale headline on black. Day: the same in the light column. Veld: the drawing drops to 48dp at 3px stroke in #1B2632, headline drops from display 40 to title.l 22/600 (a 40px headline in Veld's 24dp gutter wraps to four lines), body 17/600, and the secondary becomes full-width at 64dp — outdoors, an intrinsic-width button is a small target.
items.accessibility: The drawing is Semantics-excluded (decorative); the headline is Semantics(header: true); the region announces as one sentence followed by the action. Nothing depends on colour. At 2.0× the headline wraps freely and the whole block grows downward; because it is left-aligned and top-anchored rather than vertically centred, growth never pushes it off-screen — which is the practical reason the direction bans centred empty states, not only an aesthetic one.
items.amber: none. No TorchClaim. An absence is not a light source.
items.screenshot: A simple two-line drawing of an empty shelf at the left gutter, beneath it 'Route done.' in large warm off-white, then a quieter line reading '8 of 8 visited' with the figures in a monospaced face.

items.name: Error state
items.purpose: A failure the user can act on, told as what happened and what to do — including the session-ended case, which is a state, not an error.
items.anatomy: The same left-aligned skeleton as the empty state and deliberately so, because an error is a kind of emptiness. The 64dp 2px-stroke drawing, from the same closed enum, in bad rather than edge-control, with a filled triangle at its lower-right. Headline at title.l — what failed, in the user's terms ('Could not reach the server'). Body at body ink-2 — what it means for their work, always naming the work's safety first: 'Your 6 sections are safe on this phone.' Then, where a technical detail exists, a meta line in mono.ident carrying the code ('HTTP 503') for support. Then a primary or secondary action.
items.states: NETWORK FAILURE: 'No signal' + 'Your work is held on this phone and sends itself' + no retry button (a retry with no signal is theatre) + a Held flag chip. SERVER FAILURE (5xx): 'The server is having trouble' + 'Your work is held' + a Retry primary. REJECTED (4xx): 'The server would not take this' + the specific reason + a Fix action that opens the offending field; never a bare Retry, because retrying an unchanged rejection fails identically. TOO LARGE (413): 'This photo is too big to send as it is' + 'We will resize it and try again' + a Retry primary. SESSION ENDED (401/403) — REVISED, and the critic is right twice over. This is NOT the error treatment: it is a full-screen STATE, drawing in edge-control not bad, headline 'You have been signed out', body 'Your 6 sections and 3 photos are still on this phone'. The first draft then rendered the live screen behind it at 0.35 opacity 'so she can see it survived' — which measures 2.84:1, below 3:1 even for large text, and which is a full-screen Opacity over a live widget tree, meaning a full-screen saveLayer: the most expensive frame in the app, spent making its own reassurance illegible. THE PROOF IS NOW COUNTABLE, NOT GHOSTLY: the decision sheet's proof block renders inline at full contrast — a well-filled outlined box listing '6 of 9 sections captured', '3 photos held on this phone', 'Started 08:14', figures in JBM, section-state glyphs leading each line. Zero opacity layers, zero saveLayer, and a stronger claim than a picture of a screen. Primary action 'Sign in to send them'. No triangle, no crimson, no 'error'. PERMISSION DENIED: what the permission buys plus a button into Settings. UNKNOWN: 'Something went wrong' plus the code in mono.ident plus a Retry — and it is logged, because an unknown that recurs is a ticket. PARTIAL: where some content loaded, the error renders as an inline soft row at the failure's place in the list, not as a whole screen.
items.behaviour: Retry shows the button's busy state in place; the error block does not disappear and reappear. Repeated failure adds a count in meta ('Tried 3 times') rather than repeating the same message. Buzz.warning on first appearance only, never on a retry loop.
items.modes: Night: a crimson line drawing and pale type on black. Day: the darker crimson column on paper. Veld: 48dp 3px drawing in #7A0F22, headline 22/600, body 17/600, the mono code line dropped entirely (a support code is unreadable in glare and useless to an agent on a shelf), action full-width 64dp.
items.accessibility: Semantics(liveRegion: true) announcing headline then body, so the work's safety is heard second and never missed. The triangle plus the wording carry the failure with no colour dependency. The session-ended state deliberately has no alert semantics — it is announced politely, because it is not an emergency — and its proof block is a focusable list, so a screen-reader user can walk her own held work item by item. At 2.0× everything wraps and grows downward from a top anchor.
items.amber: none from the block itself. Where it carries a primary action, that action declares TorchClaim.primaryCommit like any other. There is no amber warning in TradeIQ, and a failure is the single most tempting place to break that rule.
items.screenshot: A rose-toned line drawing of a broken envelope at the left gutter, 'Could not reach the server' in bold beneath it, then 'Your 6 sections are safe on this phone' in grey, a small monospaced 'HTTP 503', and an outlined 'Retry' button.

items.name: Offline / held banner
items.purpose: The persistent statement of what is on this phone and what it is doing — the sync chip, promoted into a real component.
items.anatomy: A full-width soft row, COMPACT density (min-height 56), sitting directly beneath the header on every agent screen, gutter-aligned, radius 14, fill well, 1px edge-structure outline in Night. Leading 20dp silhouette. Title at body.strong 15/600 ink-1 with the count in JBM. Subtitle at meta 12/400 ink-3. Trailing 20dp chevron. The whole banner is tappable to My work.
items.states: ALL SENT — 1px good border, filled-circle glyph, 'Everything sent', subtitle 'Last sent 12 minutes ago'. After 4 seconds it collapses to nothing at 320ms/exit; a permanent green banner is noise. HELD (the normal state) — Oatmeal on the well, filled-square glyph, '12 captures held on this phone', subtitle 'They will send themselves · nothing is lost'. Deliberately NOT a severity and never crimson: towers go down with the grid and '12 held' is a normal Tuesday. SENDING — the square glyph pulses on the 3200ms loop where the claim is granted, otherwise it is static, 'Sending 12 captures', subtitle 'Do not close the app' only where that is actually true, otherwise 'You can close the app'. NEEDS YOU — 3px bad left bar, filled triangle, '2 items need you', subtitle naming the first reason; the only state that raises a colour. OFFLINE ENTIRELY — a broken-cloud glyph, 'No signal', subtitle 'Work is held here until signal returns'. PAUSED — hollow square, 'Paused to save data', with a 'Send now' tertiary. UNKNOWN — the banner does not render at all. It never guesses, and it never claims everything is fine.
items.behaviour: State changes cross-fade at 200ms; the count animates with AnimatedCount. It never animates its own height — every state is 56dp so content beneath does not jump. Tap opens My work with Buzz.tick. It is never dismissible: held work is a standing fact.
items.modes: Night: a quiet warm-grey banner on the well. Day: the same in the light column. Veld: 72dp, radius 0, 2px #1B2632 border, title 17/600, subtitle 14/600 in #4A4437, glyphs at 3px stroke, needs-you a solid #7A0F22 block with white ink, and NO pulse in the sending state — the word 'Sending' plus a static filled square.
items.accessibility: REVISED, and the critic found the worst accessibility bug in the kit. liveRegion was on the whole banner with the count inside its label, and the count animates — so an agent capturing twelve items during a visit heard '13 captures held on this phone, tap to open your work' interrupt her mid-sentence twelve times, during the one workflow where interruption loses data. NOW: Semantics(button: true, label: '<state sentence>, tap to open your work', value: '<count> captures') and liveRegion scoped to a child node carrying ONLY the state word, which changes six times in a day rather than twelve times in a visit. The count lives in the node's value, read on focus, and never in the live label. Announcements debounce to one per 5 seconds. Six distinct silhouettes — circle, square, pulsing square, triangle, broken cloud, hollow square — so every state is distinguishable in greyscale; the pulse degrades to the word under reduce-motion. At 2.0× the banner grows to intrinsic height and both lines wrap; the chevron stays on the first line.
items.amber: declares TorchClaim.livePulse, precedence 5, Night only, and only while genuinely sending. Held is Oatmeal, not amber; this is the single most common place the brand would otherwise leak into a status.
items.screenshot: A soft dark outlined bar under the header with a small filled square at its left, the words '12 captures held on this phone' in warm off-white, beneath them 'They will send themselves · nothing is lost' in grey, and a chevron at the right.

items.name: Section divider
items.purpose: Two jobs kept apart: separating peers inside a list, and naming a new region of a screen.
items.anatomy:
PLAIN DIVIDER — 1px hairline-decorative (#3A4B60 Night / #DED7C9 Day), full width of its container, no insets inside a panel, gutter-inset inside a scrolling list. Decorative only: never the sole identifier of anything and never the only cue that two regions differ — which is now a rule the whole kit obeys, because rows carry their own edges and no longer lean on dividers to be findable.
KNOCKED-OUT RULE (the section marker, and the direction's replacement for uppercase eyebrows as a universal marker) — a 1px hairline across the full width with the section's name sitting ON it at the leading gutter, at title.m 16/600 ink-1, ground knocked out 12dp either side of the text. No uppercase, no eyebrow, no number, no icon. The name says what the section demands — 'Needs a decision', 'Held', 'Not started' — never '01 / Overview'.
SPACING — 40dp above a knocked-out rule, 20dp below it. A plain divider takes no margin; the rows' own padding provides it.
items.states: Default. With a count: the count in JBM figure.s ink-2 after the name with a 12dp gap, inside the same knock-out. With an action: a tertiary at the trailing end, on the rule, with its own 12dp knock-out. Sticky: a knocked-out rule may pin to the top of a scroll region — its knock-out then becomes an opaque ground-filled bar the full width, so text passing beneath it is cleanly cut. Empty section: the rule still renders, with the count as 0 and the empty state beneath — a section that hides when empty makes the emptiness invisible. Loading: the rule and the name render, the count is a 24×16 skeleton block.
items.behaviour: Nothing animates. A sticky rule's transition into pinned state is an instant opacity swap of its knock-out fill, not a fade, so no frame shows text half-cut.
items.modes: Night: a barely-there cool line with a bright name sitting on it. Day: a warm line with a dark name. Veld: the plain divider becomes a 2px #1B2632 rule; the knocked-out rule becomes a 2px rule with the name at 18/600 ABOVE it rather than on it, with a 12dp gap — knocking a 2px rule out around 18/600 text in glare produces a ragged edge, and a name above a heavy rule reads better.
items.accessibility: A knocked-out rule is Semantics(header: true) with the section name plus its count, so screen-reader users can navigate by section. A plain divider is Semantics-excluded entirely. At 2.0× the name wraps to two lines and the rule sits behind the first line only, with the knock-out sized to the widest line; Veld's above-the-rule form handles this without any special case, which is part of why it exists.
items.amber: none. No TorchClaim.
items.screenshot: A thin line running the full width of a black screen with the words 'Needs a decision' sitting astride it at the left, the line stopping cleanly a little before and after the text.

items.name: Progress bar
items.purpose: Progress with a known end: a route, an upload, a capture ladder, and the gap list's progress-to-reward.
items.anatomy:
DETERMINATE — track 8dp (up from 6 to give the outline room), radius 4, fill lifted #2C3B4D AND a 1px edge-structure #5A7088 outline in Night — REVISED, because lifted on ground measures 1.67:1 and a track you cannot see cannot state a proportion; the toggle's OFF track and the count stepper already carried borders and this did not. Progress fill chart-neutral #8B8271 (3.01:1 on the track, 5.02:1 on ground), inset 1px inside the outline, with a hard leading edge. Above it a label row: the name at label 13/500 ink-2 left, the fraction in JBM figure.s right — '6/9', '14 of 20 visits'. 8dp between the label row and the track.
PROGRESS-TO-REWARD variant — the same 8dp track plus milestone notches: 2dp vertical ticks in ink-3 at each threshold, and the reward threshold marked by a 3dp notch that BREAKS the track's top edge by 3dp so it has a silhouette rather than only a hue. A label beneath the reward notch at meta ink-3 in JBM — 'R500 at 20 visits'. Past-threshold progress continues to fill beyond it.
INDETERMINATE — a 2dp Oatmeal rule travelling the track on the 1400ms linear loop (the skeleton's mechanism, reused, so the app has one 'working' motion, not two).
items.states: Zero: the track renders empty with the fraction '0/9' — never hidden, because zero progress is information, and the outline is what makes an empty track visible as a track. Determinate. Complete: the fill reaches the end and the fraction is replaced by the word 'Done' at body.strong in good; the bar does not disappear. Indeterminate. Stalled (no progress for 10s during an upload): the travelling rule stops, the track keeps its current fill, and a meta line reads 'Stuck at 40% · tap to retry'. Failed: the filled portion takes a 45° hatch in bad (hard-stop LinearGradient stripes, no blur) and stops; the unfilled portion stays as track. The hatch, not the hue, is the encoding. Unknown total: the bar renders indeterminate with the label alone; it never invents a denominator. Reward reached: the notch's tick fills solid and the label beneath becomes 'R500 earned' at body.strong; nothing pulses and nothing celebrates in colour.
items.behaviour: Progress animates to its new value over 320ms/state, and never backwards — a value that decreases is set instantly, because a reversing progress bar reads as a bug. Upload progress updates at most 4×/second. The travelling rule is driven by the shared Ticker.
items.modes: Night as specified, with the outline. Day: track #E2DBCC, fill ink-3 #676052 (4.52:1 on track), no outline needed. Veld: track white with a 2px #1B2632 border, fill solid #1B2632, 10dp tall, notches 3dp full-height with a filled triangle above the reward threshold, fraction at JBM 18/600, and no travelling rule at all — an indeterminate bar in Veld renders as the word 'Working' at 17/600.
items.accessibility: Semantics(value: '6 of 9', label: '<what>') on a progress role; indeterminate announces 'working' rather than a percentage. The fraction always renders as text beside the bar — the bar is never the only statement of progress. The failed state is a hatch plus a word, never crimson alone. At 2.0× the label row wraps to two lines and the track keeps its height; the track is a graphic and does not scale.
items.amber: NONE, in any skin, in any state — REVISED, the near-reward exception is deleted. The first draft let the leading 12dp of the fill take an amber bloom 'when the agent is within one step of the reward', arguing the bar was then the expected next move. The critic is right and the argument was self-serving: a progress bar is not a move, it is a report, and 'you are nearly there' is an achievement status — precisely what the law forbids. Worse, it lit a scoreboard on a screen where the tappable commit action was then the least lit thing on it. The near-reward moment now uses the treatment already specified for Day and Veld in all three skins: the leading segment goes solid ink-1 with a filled triangle at its head, which survives greyscale and glare and costs nothing. If the moment deserves more, it belongs in the row's sentence — 'one visit to R500' — not in the hue. No TorchClaim.
items.screenshot: A thin dark track outlined in a faint cool line with a warm-grey fill reaching about two-thirds across, its leading edge solid pale with a small triangle at its head, a tick breaking the track's top edge near the right end, '14 of 20 visits' in monospaced type above and 'R500 at 20 visits' in small grey beneath the tick.

items.name: Meter
items.purpose: A value against a target, small enough to live inside a stat cell or a row — the compact cousin of the ranked bar, and the shape the gap list's stat tile should be built from.
items.anatomy: Track 6dp (up from 3, for the same reason as the progress bar — a 1px outline needs interior), radius 3, full width of its cell, fill lifted #2C3B4D with a 1px edge-structure outline in Night. Value fill chart-neutral #8B8271, inset 1px. TARGET TICK: 2dp wide at the target's position, extending 2dp ABOVE the track's top edge so it has a silhouette in greyscale — a tick that is only a hue change is invisible. Default tick colour is ink-1. 6dp above the meter, the figure in JBM figure.l 32/600 with its eyebrow at 11/700 ink-2 above that; 4dp below, the target in meta ink-3 — 'target 85%'.
items.states: ON TARGET (value ≥ target): value fill switches to good, and a filled circle is drawn at the fill's leading edge. The circle is the signal; the hue is the confirmation. BELOW TARGET: fill stays chart-neutral, a half-filled triangle leads it, and the shortfall renders in the meta line — '61% · 24 points under'. WELL BELOW: fill takes a 45° bad hatch, a filled triangle leads it, and the owning row takes a 3px bad left bar. OVER-TARGET: the fill continues past the tick to the track's end and the overflow is hatched in good — over-performance reads as different, not as merely full. NO DATA: the track renders as an EMPTY OUTLINED track with no fill at all, the figure above it is an em dash in ink-3, and the meta line reads 'no visits in this window'. Never a zero-length fill presented as a zero value, never a delta arrow beside nothing. The outline is what makes this state work at all — the critic is right that a 3dp 1.67:1 empty track was indistinguishable from no meter, so 'we have no visits' and 'this cell has no meter' looked identical; an outlined empty track is unmistakably a meter with nothing in it. NO TARGET SET: no tick, meta line 'no target'; the value still renders. LOADING: an outlined empty track plus a figure-sized skeleton block. UNMEASURED DIMENSION (the outcome breakdown's case): em dash plus a fully hatched track — the hatch says 'we did not look', the empty track says 'we looked and found nothing', and the two are now visually distinct at arm's length.
items.behaviour: The fill animates from 0 at 600ms/ease-out-quart on first paint, once per visible cluster from a single AnimationController, not one per meter. It does not re-animate on rebuild. Values that change animate at 320ms/state.
items.modes: Night as specified, with the outline. Day: track #E2DBCC, fill ink-3, tick ink-1 #1B2632. Veld: 8dp track with a 2px #1B2632 border, fill solid #1B2632, tick a 4dp full-height break plus a filled triangle above the track, figure at JBM 24/600, hatch stripes thickened to 4dp on / 4dp off.
items.accessibility: Semantics(label: '<name>', value: '61 percent, target 85 percent, 24 points under target') — the relationship is spoken, not inferred from a picture. Four leading-edge silhouettes (circle, half triangle, filled triangle, nothing) plus the hatch carry every state without colour. The em-dash state announces 'not measured, no visits in this window'. At 2.0× the figure scales, the meter keeps its 6dp height, and a 2×2 cluster collapses to 1×4 on a LayoutBuilder width threshold.
items.amber: declares TorchClaim.meterTick, precedence 6 — the bottom of the ladder, one meter per route, Night only, and only the meter the screen's headline sentence is about. Denied, which is the common case on a tabbed route, the tick is ink-1 with the identical silhouette and nothing is lost.
items.screenshot: A large monospaced '61%' with a small grey label above it, beneath them a thin dark track outlined in a faint cool line, filled two-thirds in warm grey with a half-triangle at the fill's head and a small pale tick standing proud of the track near the right, and 'target 85%' in small grey below.

items.name: Focus, press and haptics
items.purpose: The cross-cutting rules for how every control in the kit responds to a finger, a keyboard, a switch and a screen reader.
items.anatomy:
FOCUS RING — 2px flame-700 #FFCB94 at a 2dp offset outside the control's own border, following the control's radius (Night: 10.38:1 on surface, 9.11:1 on raised). Day: 2px ink-1 #1B2632 at a 2dp offset. Veld: 3px #0E141A at a 3dp offset. It renders only under keyboard, switch-access or D-pad navigation — Flutter's FocusManager.highlightMode — never on a touch tap, so a field tapped with a thumb does not sprout a ring.
PRESS — every pressable surface scales to 0.98 (small glyph targets to 0.94) at 120ms/state, plus a fill change to a DECLARED FLATTENED TOKEN, never an alpha multiplier: press-ghost-night #18212D on transparent controls, lifted #2C3B4D on filled ones. Scale plus fill are two channels, so a press is never colour-only.
HAPTICS — Buzz.tick (light) on every ordinary selection, step and press; Buzz.finding (a distinct double) on a zero that is a finding; Buzz.warning (medium) on a destructive first press and on a failure toast; Buzz.success (light double) on a completed commit. Nothing else vibrates. Repeat-rate steps drop to every fifth haptic.
items.states: Focused. Focused-and-pressed: ring stays, fill changes, scale applies. Disabled: never focusable and never pressable — it is skipped in the focus order rather than focusable-and-dead. Focus on a scrolled-out control: the scroll region brings it into view with a 16dp margin at 200ms before the ring draws.
items.behaviour: Focus order follows visual order, which on every screen in this system is top-to-bottom in one left-aligned column — the left alignment rule is what makes the focus order trivially correct. Thumb-zone actions are last in the order, never first. A route that opens with a keyboard-focusable field focuses the field; every other route focuses its header.
items.modes: The amber focus ring is Night-only. Day and Veld use ink, because on a light ground a 1.79:1 amber ring is invisible in Veld and would spend the one amber block in Day.
items.accessibility: This pattern is the reason the kit can claim 'colour is never the only signal' for interaction state: press is scale + fill, focus is a 2–3px ring with a real contrast figure, selection is fill + weight + a mark, disabled is ink-mute + a reason line. Every one of those is a declared token pair, so the CI walk sees all of it — which is only true since the opacity ban. At 2.0× rings scale with the control they surround. Under reduce-motion, press scale is dropped and only the fill changes.
items.amber: the focus ring in Night — exempt from TorchScope by declaration inside TorchScope itself, not as an unstated allowance: exactly one control can hold focus, the ring is transient, and it appears only for non-touch input, so it can never co-occur with a second focus ring and never appears at all for the overwhelming majority of this app's users.
items.screenshot: A ghost button with a crisp warm amber outline floating 2dp clear of its own cool grey border, the only ringed element on an otherwise unhighlighted screen.

openQuestions:
WHAT THE CRITIC ASKED FOR AND DID NOT GET, so the owner sees the disagreement rather than discovering it. (1) The critic wants the Night nav pill to yield its amber to the primary commit per route. I refused. Yielding chrome per route makes the app's permanent furniture amber on Today and ink on Map, which reads as a rendering bug and destroys the one piece of identity owner decision 3 bought. Instead the Night nav holds a reserved chrome grant and content holds the other, which makes the law a sentence rather than a computation: the torch is in your hand and on the shelf, one each. The consequence I am accepting in exchange, and naming rather than hiding: on a Night tabbed route with BOTH a plate and a primary commit — agent outlet detail with 'Check in here' is the real one — the plate renders without its strip light. That is the Day plate treatment applied in Night. It is already specified and already tested, but it means the system's most beautiful object is dark on one of its most-used screens, and if the owner would rather lose the amber nav pill than that, the TorchScope change is one line and everything else in this kit is unaffected. (2) The critic put the plate above the primary in the precedence ladder. I inverted it: a commit action is a move and the torch shows the next move; a plate is a subject. The escape hatch is a single declared per-route `subject:` override, which exists for the Ask TradeIQ answer route, where the send field is technically a commit action but the answer is why the user is there.

THREE CONFLICTS BETWEEN THE OWNER'S DECISIONS AND THE DIRECTION SPEC, resolved here but still worth confirming. (a) TYPEFACE. The spec names Archivo Variable with a wdth 88–112 axis doing real layout work; the owner names Onest, which has no width axis, and extends JetBrains Mono to every figure in a data role. I followed the owner: wdth instructions are void, weight and tracking carry the display voice. Two consequences the spec's numbers no longer cover, and both are still open — the footprint (Onest variable ~0.4 MB replaces four Inters, but JBM Medium must stay for figures, so the net APK saving is roughly −1.2 MB, not −2.03 MB), and the hero fitting thresholds, which were measured on Archivo at wdth 112 and must be re-measured on JBM's fixed advance width. JBM is wider per digit than Archivo condensed; 'R 1,28 mln' at 72px may not fit 360dp. Someone should run that specimen before the hero thresholds are committed. (b) THE NAV PILL'S ATTRIBUTION RISK. The spec deletes the 999 radius and the active-tab pill on both plagiarism and 1.4.11 grounds; owner decision 3 reinstates them. I have fixed the accessibility half — a solid #FFB162 pill with #0B1017 ink is 10.65:1 where the reference's tint-behind-icon was 1.5–2.0:1 — and mitigated the rest by refusing to slide the pill between slots and keeping the circle outside the bar. The attribution objection stands and I cannot resolve it from here; the 3px amber underbar remains available and nothing else in this kit depends on the pill's geometry. (c) AMBER IN DAY NAVIGATION. Unchanged from the first draft and now enforced by TorchScope rather than asserted: the Day and Veld active tab is an ink block, the amber pill is Night-only, and the nav therefore looks materially different across skins. Defensible, but a decision the owner should see.

STILL OUTSTANDING, NOT CONFLICTS. The three empty-state drawings — shelf, pin, envelope — are now a closed enum, which is the whole point, but they do not exist and nobody can build the empty state until they do; they are a half-day of one illustrator and the enum will not accept a stock import. The 'provisional vs final' reconciliation line ('scored 71, you saw 84') is specified here only inside the numeric field; whichever surface owns the outcome screen must decide what happens when the two figures disagree by enough to change the rating band — my field-level treatment shows both but does not decide which band the row is filed under. And the gap list's stat tile must be built as a Meter with the track omitted rather than as its own widget, because its no-data rule is identical and a separate implementation will drift within a release.
principles: Darkness is the site; amber is emitted light, never a label. The amber law is now enforced by the framework, not by prose: a TorchScope resolves each route's declared claim set against a fixed precedence ladder and issues two grants in Night, one in Day and Veld, and every denied claimant falls back to an ink treatment it already owns. Nothing is identified by a fill step alone — Night carries identity on real 3:1 edges — and nothing is expressed by opacity, so every state is a token pair CI can walk. Severity is crimson at two commitment levels plus a silhouette plus a word. Held is Oatmeal. Onest carries words, JetBrains Mono carries every figure.
